exercises.air-squat:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, toes turned slightly out.
2. Push your hips back and lower down as if sitting into a chair.
3. Go down until your thighs are parallel to the floor or slightly below.
4. Drive through your heels and return to a full stand.
Note: Keep your back straight and chest up throughout the movement.
exercises.back-squat:
1. Rest the bar on your shoulders behind your head and grip it at a comfortable width.
2. Unrack the bar and take one step back, feet shoulder-width apart.
3. Lower with control until your thighs are parallel to the floor.
4. Drive through your heels and return to a full stand.
Note: Keep your back straight and don't let your knees cave inward.
exercises.box-jump:
1. Stand facing the box, a small step away.
2. Dip slightly by bending your knees and swing your arms back.
3. Jump and land softly with both feet in the middle of the box.
4. Stand up fully on the box.
Careful: Step down off the box backward rather than jumping down, to protect your ankles.
exercises.chair-squat:
1. Stand with your back to a sturdy chair, feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Push your hips back and lower slowly until your glutes lightly touch the seat.
3. Without relaxing onto the chair, stand straight back up, driving through your heels.
Note: Control the descent all the way down; don't drop onto the chair.
exercises.dumbbell-squat:
1. Hold a dumbbell in each hand, arms straight at your sides.
2. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and chest up.
3. Squat down until your thighs are parallel to the floor, the dumbbells lowering alongside your body.
4. Drive through your heels and stand back up.
Note: Keep your back straight and don't round your shoulders forward.
exercises.front-squat:
1. Rest the bar on the front of your shoulders, elbows lifted high and forward.
2. Unrack the bar and step back, feet shoulder-width apart.
3. Squat down while keeping your torso upright and elbows high.
4. Drive through your heels and stand back up.
Note: If your elbows drop, the bar rolls forward; keep them up the whole time.
exercises.goblet-squat:
1. Hold a dumbbell vertically in both hands, close to your chest.
2. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, elbows pointing down.
3. Squat down deep while the dumbbell stays close to your body.
4. Drive through your heels and stand back up.
Note: Keep your chest up; don't let the dumbbell pull you forward.
exercises.jump-squat:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Squat down until your thighs are almost parallel to the floor.
3. Explode upward and jump off the floor, using an arm swing.
4. Land softly and go straight into the descent of the next rep.
Note: Land on the balls of your feet with soft knees to cushion the landing.
exercises.overhead-squat:
1. Take a wide grip on the bar and bring it locked out straight overhead.
2. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, the bar over the middle of your feet.
3. Squat down slowly while your arms stay straight and the bar stays overhead.
4. Drive through your heels and stand back up.
Note: Start with an empty bar or a stick; this exercise requires a lot of shoulder mobility.
exercises.pistol-squat:
1. Stand on one leg and extend the other leg straight out in front.
2. Reach your arms forward for balance.
3. Lower slowly on the standing leg into a deep squat.
4. Push back up without putting the other foot on the floor.
5. Complete all reps on the same leg, and switch legs only at the end of the set.
Note: Keep the heel of the standing leg on the floor throughout the movement.
exercises.strap-assisted-pistol:
1. Hold the strap handles in both hands and stand on one leg with the other leg extended forward.
2. Squat down on the standing leg, using a light grip on the straps for balance.
3. Drive through your heel and stand back up. Complete the reps, then switch legs.
Note: The straps help exactly as much as you need; the less you pull with your arms, the harder the exercise.
exercises.strap-assisted-squat:
1. Hold the strap handles in both hands, elbows slightly bent, facing the anchor point.
2. Squat down deep at your own pace, with the straps supporting your balance.
3. Help yourself with your arms only as much as needed, and drive through your heels back to standing.
Note: This is the easy way to control the difficulty: less pulling with your arms = more work for your legs.
exercises.thruster:
1. Hold a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height.
2. Squat down fully while the dumbbells stay on your shoulders.
3. Stand up with momentum, and in the same single movement press the dumbbells straight overhead.
4. Lower the dumbbells back to your shoulders and start a new rep.
Note: Use the drive from your legs for the press; don't press with your arms alone.
exercises.cable-pull-through:
1. Attach a rope handle to the pulley at its lowest setting and stand with your back to the machine.
2. Grab the rope between your legs with both hands and take a step or two forward.
3. Push your hips back and tip your torso forward with a straight back; your hands are pulled back between your legs.
4. Drive your hips forward and return to an upright stand, without pulling with your arms.
Note: The whole movement comes from the hips; your back stays straight and your hands just hold the rope.
exercises.deadlift:
1. Stand with the bar over the middle of your feet, feet hip-width apart.
2. Push your hips back and grip the bar just outside your knees, chest up and back straight.
3. Push the floor away with your legs and rise to a full stand, keeping the bar close to your body.
4. Lower the bar back to the floor along the same path, with control.
Careful: Don't round your lower back; if your back rounds, reduce the weight.
exercises.dumbbell-clean:
1. Stand with both dumbbells on the floor between your feet, hips back and back straight.
2. Grip the dumbbells and push the floor away with your legs in a fast, powerful movement.
3. As the dumbbells reach chest height, drop slightly under them and catch them on your shoulders.
4. Stabilize in a full stand, lower back to the floor with control, and repeat.
Note: The dumbbells travel close to your body; the power comes from your legs and hips, not from pulling with your arms.
exercises.glute-bridge:
1. Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor, close to your glutes.
2. Place your hands on the floor at your sides.
3. Push through your heels and lift your hips until you form a straight line from knees to shoulders.
4. Squeeze your glutes at the top for a moment and lower slowly back down.
Note: Lift using your glutes and stop at a straight line; don't arch your lower back beyond that.
exercises.good-morning:
1. Rest the bar on your upper back as in a squat, feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Bend your knees slightly and push your hips back while tipping your torso forward.
3. Lower until your torso is close to parallel with the floor, with a straight back and open chest.
4. Drive your hips forward and return to an upright stand.
Careful: Start with a very light bar; a rounded back in this exercise is dangerous, so keep it straight all the way.
exercises.hip-thrust:
1. Sit on the floor with your upper back resting against a bench, and place the bar in the crease of your hips, ideally with padding.
2. Bend your knees and plant your feet firmly on the floor.
3. Push through your heels and lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from knees to shoulders.
4. Squeeze your glutes at the top and lower with control.
Note: Keep your chin close to your chest and don't arch your lower back at the top of the movement.
exercises.kettlebell-snatch:
1. Stand over the kettlebell and grip the handle with one hand, hips back and back straight.
2. Swing it back between your legs as in a swing.
3. Drive your hips forward powerfully and pull the kettlebell upward close to your body.
4. At head height, let your arm straighten and catch the kettlebell softly overhead, then lower it back down.
5. Complete all reps with one hand, and switch hands only at the end of the set.
Note: Let the kettlebell roll gently around your hand; don't let it slam onto your forearm.
exercises.kettlebell-swing:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, the kettlebell on the floor slightly in front of you.
2. Push your hips back with a straight back, grip the handle with both hands and swing the kettlebell back between your legs.
3. Drive your hips forward powerfully so the kettlebell floats up to chest height.
4. Let it swing back down between your legs and go straight into the next rep in one continuous motion.
Note: The power comes from your hips, not your arms; keep your back straight throughout the movement.
exercises.one-arm-kettlebell-swing:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and grip the kettlebell handle with one hand.
2. Push your hips back and swing the kettlebell between your legs with a straight back.
3. Drive your hips forward powerfully and swing the kettlebell up to chest height.
4. Complete all reps with one hand, then switch hands.
Note: Keep your shoulders and hips square to the wall in front of you; don't let your torso twist with the weight.
exercises.romanian-deadlift:
1. Stand upright holding the bar in front of your thighs, knees slightly bent.
2. Push your hips back and lower the bar close to your legs.
3. Stop at about mid-shin, when you feel a stretch in your hamstrings.
4. Drive your hips forward and return to an upright stand.
Note: The movement comes from the hips only; your back stays straight and doesn't round on the way down.
exercises.single-leg-deadlift:
1. Stand on one leg with a dumbbell in the opposite hand.
2. Tip your torso forward while sending your free leg straight back.
3. Lower the dumbbell to about knee height, keeping your back straight.
4. Return to standing with control, and complete the reps before switching sides.
Note: Keep your hips square to the floor and don't rush; balance matters more than depth.
exercises.single-leg-glute-bridge:
1. Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
2. Lift one leg into the air and straighten it.
3. Push through the heel of the supporting leg and lift your hips until you form a straight line from knee to shoulders.
4. Lower slowly, and complete all reps before switching legs.
Note: Keep your hips level; don't let the side of the raised leg drop.
exercises.strap-hamstring-curl:
1. Lie on your back and place your heels in the strap handles, legs straight.
2. Lift your hips off the floor into a straight line from shoulders to heels.
3. Bend your knees and pull your heels toward your glutes, without dropping your hips.
4. Slowly return your legs to full extension.
Note: Your hips stay up the whole set; if they drop, do only the hip lift for now.
exercises.bench-dips:
1. Sit on the edge of a sturdy chair and place your hands beside your thighs, fingers gripping the edge.
2. Slide your hips forward off the chair, legs out in front.
3. Bend your elbows and lower your hips toward the floor.
4. Push back up until your arms are straight.
Careful: Keep your back close to the chair and don't go deep if you have shoulder pain.
exercises.bench-press:
1. Lie on the bench with your eyes under the bar and grip slightly wider than shoulder-width.
2. Unrack the bar and straighten your arms over your chest.
3. Lower the bar with control until it lightly touches your chest.
4. Press back up until your arms are fully straight.
Careful: Don't lift heavy without a spotter nearby.
exercises.cable-crossover:
1. Hold a handle in each hand from the two high sides of the cable machine, and take a step forward.
2. Lean your torso slightly forward, arms open to the sides with elbows slightly bent.
3. Bring your hands toward each other in a wide arc until they meet in front of your chest.
4. Open back out to the sides in a controlled movement, without losing the slight bend in your elbows.
Note: Your elbows stay slightly bent and fixed; the entire movement comes from the shoulders, not the elbows.
exercises.decline-pushup:
1. Place your feet on a sturdy chair and your hands on the floor at shoulder-width.
2. Lower your chest toward the floor with control, elbows close to your body.
3. Push back up until your arms are fully straight.
Note: Keep your neck neutral and don't let your head drop toward the floor.
exercises.dips:
1. Grip both bars and rise into a support position with straight arms and a stable body.
2. Bend your elbows and slowly lower your body until your shoulders are level with your elbows.
3. Push back up until your arms are fully straight.
Careful: Don't go too deep if you feel pressure in your shoulders.
exercises.dumbbell-bench-press:
1. Lie on your back on a bench, a dumbbell in each hand at chest level, feet on the floor.
2. Press the dumbbells up until your arms are fully straight over your chest.
3. Lower with control back to chest level.
Note: Don't arch your back; keep your feet planted on the floor throughout the set.
exercises.dumbbell-floor-press:
1. Lie on your back on the floor with knees bent, a dumbbell in each hand close to your chest.
2. Press the dumbbells up until your arms are fully straight over your chest.
3. Lower slowly until your elbows lightly touch the floor.
Note: Set your elbows down gently on the floor, without slamming them.
exercises.incline-pushup:
1. Place your hands on a stable surface at shoulder-width, and walk your feet back until your body forms a straight line.
2. Bend your elbows and lower your chest toward the surface with control.
3. Push back up until your arms are fully straight.
Note: Keep your body straight the whole way, without letting your hips sag.
exercises.pushup:
1. Place your hands on the floor at shoulder-width, legs straight behind you and body in one line.
2. Lower your body as one unit until your chest almost touches the floor.
3. Push back up until your arms are fully straight.
Note: Brace your abs and don't let your lower back sag.
exercises.strap-pushup:
1. Hold the strap handles and get into a push-up position, hands on the handles and body in a straight line.
2. Bend your elbows and lower your chest between the handles, controlling the wobble.
3. Push back up without losing your body line.
Note: Control the difficulty through the angle: the more upright your body, the easier; the more horizontal, the harder.
exercises.triceps-pushdown:
1. Attach a short bar or rope to the pulley above head height, and stand facing it.
2. Grip the handle with your elbows bent and tucked at your sides.
3. Straighten your elbows and push the handle down until your arms are fully straight.
4. Let it rise slowly until your forearms are parallel to the floor, without your elbows moving.
Note: Only your forearms move; your elbows stay glued to your sides.
exercises.dumbbell-shoulder-press:
1. Stand upright, a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height, palms facing forward.
2. Press the dumbbells up until your arms are fully straight overhead.
3. Lower slowly and with control back to shoulder height.
Note: Brace your abs and don't arch your lower back while pressing.
exercises.handstand-pushup:
1. Kick up into a handstand with your heels resting against a wall and your hands shoulder-width apart.
2. Bend your elbows and slowly lower your head until it almost touches the floor.
3. Push back up until your arms are fully straight.
Careful: This is a very advanced exercise; do it only if you have full control of the descent, and come down off the wall as soon as you lose control.
exercises.kettlebell-push-press:
1. Bring a kettlebell to shoulder height, with your elbow tucked against your body and the weight resting on your forearm.
2. Dip into a short, quick knee bend.
3. Drive with your legs and straighten your arm to a lockout overhead.
4. Lower with control back to your shoulder, and switch sides at the end of the set.
Note: At the lockout, the weight should be over the center of your body, not in front.
exercises.pike-pushup:
1. Start in a push-up position and lift your hips high so your body forms an upside-down V.
2. Bend your elbows and slowly lower the top of your head toward the floor.
3. Push back up until your arms are fully straight.
Note: Keep your gaze toward your feet so you don't strain your neck.
exercises.push-press:
1. Rest the bar on your upper chest, elbows slightly in front of the bar.
2. Dip into a short, quick knee bend with your torso upright.
3. Drive powerfully with your legs and continue by straightening your arms until the bar is locked out overhead.
4. Lower the bar back to your chest with control.
Note: Keep your heels on the ground during the dip; it's a short dip, not a squat.
exercises.shoulder-press:
1. Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width and rest it on your upper chest.
2. Press the bar up in a straight line until your arms are fully straight.
3. Move your head slightly back as the bar passes your face.
4. Lower the bar with control back to your chest.
Note: Squeeze your abs and glutes throughout the movement so you don't arch your back.
exercises.band-assisted-pullup:
1. Loop a resistance band around the pull-up bar and place a foot or knee into the loop.
2. Hang from the bar with a grip slightly wider than your shoulders.
3. Pull yourself up until your chin clears the bar.
4. Lower slowly until your arms are fully straight.
Careful: Release your foot from the band carefully at the end of the set so it doesn't snap free suddenly.
exercises.chinup:
1. Grip the bar with palms facing you, at shoulder-width.
2. Pull yourself up until your chin clears the bar.
3. Lower slowly until your arms are fully straight.
Note: Avoid swinging your body; go up and down with control.
exercises.lat-pulldown:
1. Sit facing the machine and secure your knees under the pad.
2. Grip the bar wider than your shoulders.
3. Pull the bar to your upper chest while drawing your shoulder blades down.
4. Return slowly upward until your arms are straight.
Note: Don't lean back hard; keep your back upright and stable.
exercises.muscle-up:
1. Grip the bar slightly wider than your shoulders, thumbs over the bar.
2. Pull hard and fast until your chest reaches bar height.
3. Roll your chest over the bar and bring your elbows up into a support position.
4. Straighten your arms at the top, then lower with control in reverse order.
Note: This is a very advanced exercise; work on it only when your pull-ups and dips are strong and feel easy.
exercises.pullup:
1. Grip the bar with palms facing away from you, slightly wider than your shoulders.
2. Pull your chest toward the bar until your chin clears it.
3. Lower slowly to a full hang with straight arms.
Note: Start every rep from fully straight arms, without jumping off the ground.
exercises.scapular-pullup:
1. Hang from a pull-up bar with straight arms and a shoulder-width grip.
2. Without bending your elbows, pull your shoulder blades down and back so your body rises slightly.
3. Pause for a second at the top and return to a full hang with control.
Note: Keep your arms straight throughout the movement; the power comes from your shoulder blades only.
exercises.straight-arm-pulldown:
1. Stand facing a high pulley and grip a straight bar with both hands at shoulder-width.
2. Take a step back and lean your torso slightly forward, arms straight up and forward.
3. Without bending your elbows, pull the bar down in an arc to your thighs.
4. Let the bar rise back slowly until you feel a full stretch overhead.
Note: Your arms stay straight; the entire movement comes from the shoulders and back.
exercises.bent-over-row:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and grip the bar with an overhand grip.
2. Bend your knees slightly and tip your torso forward with a straight back.
3. Pull the bar to your lower belly with your elbows close to your body.
4. Lower slowly until your arms are straight.
Careful: Don't round your lower back; keep it straight throughout the set.
exercises.cable-biceps-curl:
1. Attach a straight bar to the pulley at its lowest setting and stand facing it.
2. Grip the bar with both hands using an underhand grip (palms facing up), elbows tucked against your body.
3. Bend your elbows and raise the bar to chest height.
4. Lower slowly until your arms are fully straight.
Note: Your body stays upright and stable, with no swinging of your back for help.
exercises.face-pull:
1. Attach a rope handle to the pulley at face height.
2. Grab the ends of the rope with both hands and take a step back.
3. Pull the rope toward your face while flaring your elbows out to the sides.
4. Return slowly forward with control.
Note: Use a light weight; the goal is control of the rear shoulders, not strength.
exercises.inverted-row:
1. Set a bar in the rack at waist height and lie underneath it.
2. Grip the bar at shoulder-width and tighten your body into a straight line from heels to shoulders.
3. Pull your chest to the bar.
4. Lower slowly until your arms are fully straight.
Note: Brace your abs and glutes so your hips don't sag in the middle of the movement.
exercises.one-arm-dumbbell-row:
1. Place one knee and one hand on a stable surface, with the other foot on the floor.
2. Hold a dumbbell in your free hand, hanging down.
3. Row the dumbbell to the side of your belly and lower it slowly.
4. Finish the reps and switch sides.
Note: Keep your back straight and don't twist your torso during the pull.
exercises.renegade-row:
1. Set up in a plank on two dumbbells, feet slightly wide for stability.
2. Row one dumbbell to the side of your belly while the other arm supports you.
3. Slowly lower the dumbbell to the floor.
4. Switch hands and keep alternating.
Note: Keep your hips stable; don't let them rotate during the pull.
exercises.seated-cable-row:
1. Sit facing the machine with your feet on the footrests and knees slightly bent.
2. Grip the handle and straighten your back.
3. Pull the handle to your belly while squeezing your shoulder blades back.
4. Return slowly forward without rounding your back.
Note: Don't rock your torso back and forth; the movement comes from your arms and back.
exercises.straps-row:
1. Hold the strap handles and lean back with a straight body and feet forward.
2. Pull your chest to the handles while squeezing your shoulder blades together.
3. Return slowly to straight arms without breaking your body line.
Note: The further forward your feet, the harder the exercise; pick an angle that allows full control.
exercises.bulgarian-split-squat:
1. Stand with your back to a chair and place your rear foot on it.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
3. Bend your front leg and lower your hips until your thigh is almost parallel to the floor.
4. Drive through your heel and come back up.
5. Complete all reps on the same leg, and switch legs only at the end of the set.
Note: Place your front foot far enough from the chair that your knee doesn't pass your toes.
exercises.dumbbell-lunge:
1. Stand upright with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
2. Step forward with one leg and lower your back knee toward the floor.
3. Push through your front heel and return to standing.
4. Switch legs on every rep.
Note: Keep your back upright and don't lean forward with the dumbbells.
exercises.dumbbell-step-up:
1. Hold a dumbbell in each hand and stand facing a sturdy chair or step.
2. Place one foot on the surface and drive through the heel up to a full stand.
3. Step down slowly and with control back to the floor, with the same leg staying the lead leg.
4. Complete all reps on the same leg, and switch legs only at the end of the set.
Note: Place your whole foot on the surface, not just the edge.
exercises.reverse-lunge:
1. Stand upright with a dumbbell in each hand.
2. Step back with one leg and lower your back knee almost to the floor.
3. Push through the heel of your front leg and return to standing.
4. Alternate legs.
Note: Keep your upper body stable throughout the movement.
exercises.step-up:
1. Stand facing a sturdy chair or step.
2. Step up with one leg and stand fully tall on top of it.
3. Raise the knee of the other leg to hip height, then step down slowly; the same foot stays on the surface.
4. Complete all reps on the same leg, and switch legs only at the end of the set.
Careful: Make sure the surface is stable and doesn't slip before you start.
exercises.strap-split-squat:
1. Stand with your back to the straps and place one foot in the handle behind you.
2. Hop lightly forward on your supporting leg until you're standing stable.
3. Lower your back knee down until your front thigh is parallel to the floor.
4. Push through your front heel and stand up. Complete the reps, then switch legs.
Note: The strap moves, so lower slowly and with control; it's intentionally harder than a fixed bench.
exercises.walking-lunge:
1. Stand upright with feet hip-width apart.
2. Take a big step forward and lower your back knee almost to the floor.
3. Push through your front heel, stand up, and go straight into a step with the other leg.
4. Keep moving forward like this with alternating steps.
Note: Keep your front knee over your foot and don't let it cave inward.
exercises.farmers-walk:
1. Pick up a dumbbell in each hand from the floor, with a straight back and bent knees.
2. Stand upright, shoulders pulled back and eyes forward.
3. Walk forward in short, steady steps for the distance.
4. Set the dumbbells down with control at the end.
Note: Don't let your shoulders round forward while walking.
exercises.suitcase-carry:
1. Pick up one dumbbell in one hand, the way you'd lift a suitcase.
2. Stand upright without leaning toward the weight.
3. Walk with controlled steps for the distance.
4. Switch hands and cover the same distance on the other side.
Note: Brace your abs to keep your torso straight, without leaning to the side.
exercises.cable-woodchop:
1. Attach a handle to the pulley at a high setting, and stand side-on to the machine, feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Grip the handle with both arms straight above the shoulder nearest the machine.
3. Pull diagonally across your body, from high up to outside your far hip, while rotating your torso and hips.
4. Return slowly to the starting point. Complete the reps, then switch sides.
Note: The rotation comes from your torso and hips together; your arms just guide the cable.
exercises.dead-bug:
1. Lie on your back, arms raised toward the ceiling and knees bent over your hips.
2. Slowly lower one arm back past your head and the opposite leg forward, close to the floor.
3. Return to the center and switch sides.
Note: Keep your lower back pressed into the floor throughout the exercise.
exercises.flutter-kicks:
1. Lie on your back with your arms at your sides and legs straight.
2. Lift both legs slightly off the floor.
3. Kick alternately up and down in small, fast movements, as if swimming.
Note: Keep your lower back pressed to the floor throughout the exercise.
exercises.hanging-leg-raise:
1. Hang from a pull-up bar with a shoulder-width grip, arms straight.
2. Raise your knees or straight legs to hip height or higher.
3. Lower slowly back down in a controlled movement.
Note: Avoid swinging your body; pause for a moment between reps if needed.
exercises.hollow-hold:
1. Lie on your back and press your lower back into the floor.
2. Lift your shoulders and legs slightly off the floor, arms stretched overhead.
3. Hold a shallow banana shape and keep the position.
Note: If your lower back lifts off the floor, bend your knees slightly or raise your legs higher.
exercises.l-sit:
1. Get into a support on the parallel bars with straight arms and shoulders pushed down.
2. Raise your straight legs forward until they're parallel to the floor, your body in an L shape.
3. Hold the position with your abs working and legs together.
Note: Knees bent toward your chest is a great starting point; straighten them gradually.
exercises.lying-leg-raise:
1. Lie on your back with legs straight and arms at your sides.
2. Raise your straight legs until they point straight up at the ceiling.
3. Lower them slowly without touching the floor.
Note: Keep your lower back pressed to the floor; if it lifts, reduce the range of motion.
exercises.machine-chest-press:
1. Sit in the machine with the handles at mid-chest height and your back against the pad.
2. Grip the handles and press forward until your arms are almost fully straight.
3. Return slowly until your elbows are slightly behind your body line.
Note: Your shoulders stay down and back; don't shrug them toward your ears as you press.
exercises.mountain-climbers:
1. Set up in a push-up position with arms straight under your shoulders.
2. Bring one knee toward your chest.
3. Return it back and switch legs at a fast pace, like running in place.
Note: Keep your hips low and back straight throughout the exercise.
exercises.pallof-press:
1. Attach a single handle to the pulley at chest height, and stand side-on to the machine.
2. Hold the handle with both hands against your chest, and step sideways until the cable is taut.
3. Press your hands straight out in front of the center of your chest, without your torso rotating.
4. Hold for a second or two and bring your hands back to your chest with control. Complete the reps, then switch sides.
Note: The cable will try to rotate you; the job is to stay completely stable.
exercises.parallel-bar-knee-raise:
1. Get into a support on the parallel bars with straight arms, a stable body and feet off the ground.
2. Pull your knees to your chest in a controlled movement, without swinging.
3. Lower your legs slowly until fully straight.
Note: Your shoulders stay pushed down; don't let your body sink between your arms.
exercises.plank:
1. Lie face down and rest on your forearms and toes, elbows under your shoulders.
2. Lift your body so it forms a straight line from shoulders to heels.
3. Brace your abs and hold the position without moving.
Note: Don't let your hips sag; keep your back straight throughout the hold.
exercises.russian-twist:
1. Sit on the floor with knees bent and lean your torso slightly back.
2. Clasp your hands in front of your chest and rotate your torso to one side.
3. Rotate to the other side in a controlled movement, and keep alternating.
Note: Rotate from your abs, not just your arms, and keep your back straight.
exercises.side-plank:
1. Lie on your side and rest on one forearm, with your elbow directly under your shoulder.
2. Lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from head to feet.
3. Hold the position, then switch sides.
Note: Don't let your hips drop; keep them high the whole time.
exercises.situp:
1. Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
2. Raise your upper body to a full sitting position.
3. Lower slowly back down until your shoulders touch the floor.
Note: Don't pull on your neck with your hands; the movement comes from your abs.
exercises.strap-fallout:
1. Hold the strap handles while standing, arms straight in front of your shoulders and body leaning slightly forward.
2. Roll your arms forward and up, with your body staying in a straight line and abs locked.
3. Stop before your lower back arches, and pull back to standing.
Note: Control the difficulty through the angle; a small step back with your feet makes it easier right away.
exercises.strap-knee-tuck:
1. Place your feet in the strap handles and get into a plank on your hands.
2. Pull your knees to your chest while your hips stay stable.
3. Slowly return your legs to a straight line.
Note: Don't let your lower back sag as you straighten your legs; your abs stay locked.
exercises.superman:
1. Lie face down with your arms stretched forward.
2. Lift your arms, chest and legs off the floor at the same time.
3. Hold for a second at the top and lower slowly back down.
Note: Lift smoothly and don't throw your head back.
exercises.turkish-getup:
1. Lie on your back holding a dumbbell in a straight arm over your chest, with the knee on the same side bent.
2. Rise gradually: prop up on the opposite elbow, then on your hand, lift your hips and sweep your straight leg back into a kneel.
3. Stand up fully while the dumbbell stays locked out overhead.
4. Go back down through the same steps in reverse order.
5. Complete all reps on one side, and switch sides only at the end of the set.
Note: Start with a very light weight and keep your eyes on the dumbbell as you rise.
exercises.burpee:
1. From standing, drop into a squat and place your hands on the floor.
2. Jump your feet back into a push-up position and lower your chest to the floor.
3. Push yourself up and jump your feet back to your hands.
4. Stand up and finish with a small jump, hands overhead.
Note: Keep your abs braced so your lower back doesn't sag.
exercises.fast-skipping:
1. Stand upright with elbows bent at a right angle.
2. Run in place while lifting your knees to hip height.
3. Pump your arms quickly in time with your legs.
4. Stay on the balls of your feet throughout the exercise.
Note: Keep your torso upright and don't lean back.
exercises.jump-rope:
1. Hold a handle in each hand with the rope resting behind you.
2. Turn the rope with small wrist movements, elbows close to your body.
3. Jump low on the balls of your feet as the rope passes under you.
4. Keep a steady rhythm and regular breathing.
Note: Land softly and low to avoid straining your knees.
exercises.jumping-jacks:
1. Stand upright with feet together and arms at your sides.
2. Jump while spreading your legs to the sides and raising your arms overhead.
3. Jump back to the starting position.
4. Keep going at a steady pace.
Note: Land softly on the balls of your feet with knees slightly bent.
exercises.rowing-machine:
1. Sit on the machine, tighten the straps over your feet and grip the handle with both hands.
2. Push hard with your legs while keeping your back straight.
3. At the end of the push, pull the handle to your lower belly.
4. Return in reverse order: straighten your arms forward and only then bend your knees.
Note: The power comes from your legs, not from pulling with your back.
exercises.band-pull-apart:
1. Hold a band stretched out in front of you at shoulder height, arms straight.
2. Pull both ends outward until your arms are fully out to the sides and your shoulder blades come together.
3. Return slowly to the starting position.
Note: Keep your hands at shoulder height throughout the movement, without shrugging your shoulders.
exercises.band-good-morning:
1. Stand on the band with feet shoulder-width apart, the other end resting on the back of your neck.
2. Keep your knees slightly bent and hinge forward from the hips until your torso is almost parallel to the floor.
3. Return to an upright stand while squeezing your glutes.
Note: Keep your back straight throughout the movement; the movement comes from the hips, not the lower back.
exercises.band-squat:
1. Stand on the band with feet shoulder-width apart, holding the ends at shoulder height.
2. Squat down while keeping constant tension in the band.
3. Drive through your heels and return to a full stand.
Note: Don't let the band go slack at the bottom of the movement.
exercises.band-shoulder-press:
1. Stand on the band with a handle in each hand at shoulder height.
2. Press both hands up until your arms are fully straight overhead.
3. Return slowly to the starting position.
Note: Don't over-arch your lower back while pressing.
exercises.band-bench-press:
1. Anchor the band behind you at chest height and hold the ends at chest height.
2. Press both hands forward until your arms are fully straight.
3. Return slowly while keeping full control of the band.
Note: Keep a stable stance so your body doesn't get pulled back by the band.
exercises.band-upright-row:
1. Stand on the band with both hands holding the ends in front of your thighs.
2. Pull your elbows up and out until your hands are at chest height.
3. Lower slowly back down.
Note: Lead with your elbows, not your wrists.
exercises.band-lateral-walk:
1. Place a band above your knees or ankles and stand in a half-squat.
2. Step to one side while keeping tension in the band, then bring the other foot partway in.
3. Continue for a set distance, then come back in the opposite direction.
Note: Keep your knees pointing forward, without letting them cave inward.
exercises.star-jump:
1. Stand in a half-squat with your arms close to your body.
2. Jump up while spreading your legs and arms out to the sides like a star.
3. Land back in a half-squat.
Note: Land softly on the balls of your feet with knees slightly bent.
exercises.lateral-bound:
1. Stand on one leg with a slight knee bend.
2. Jump sideways and land on the other leg, absorbing softly through the knee.
3. Keep alternating from side to side.
Note: Keep your knee lined up over your toes when landing, without letting it collapse inward.
exercises.standing-long-jump:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and bend your knees while swinging your arms back.
2. Jump forward with full power, landing on both feet together.
3. Absorb the landing with bent knees and stand up tall.
Note: Take full recovery between jumps; this is a jump for maximum distance, not a continuous set.
exercises.wind-sprints:
1. Mark a start line and a finish line a set distance apart (about 20-40 meters).
2. Run at maximum speed from line to line.
3. Walk back to the start as rest before the next rep.
Careful: Warm up well before sprinting to prevent a muscle injury.
exercises.split-jump:
1. Stand in a lunge position with one leg forward and one back.
2. Jump up and switch your legs in the air.
3. Land with bent knees and go straight into the next rep.
Note: Keep your torso upright and land softly to protect your knees.
exercises.reverse-crunch:
1. Lie on your back with your arms at your sides and knees bent over your belly.
2. Contract your abs and lift your glutes off the floor, bringing your knees toward your chest.
3. Lower slowly back to the starting position.
Note: Lift by contracting your abs, not with momentum from your legs.
exercises.air-bike:
1. Lie on your back with your hands behind your head and knees bent in the air.
2. Bring your elbow toward the opposite knee while straightening the other leg.
3. Switch sides continuously, like pedaling a bicycle.
Note: Lead with the rotation of your torso, not by pulling your head with your hands.
exercises.cable-crunch:
1. Kneel facing the cable machine, grab the rope overhead and pull it down to face height.
2. Contract your abs and curl your torso forward and down, bringing your elbows toward your knees.
3. Return slowly to the starting position while keeping tension on the cable.
Note: The movement comes from contracting your abs, not from bending back at the hips.
exercises.cable-russian-twist:
1. Sit or stand beside the cable machine and hold the handle with both hands in front of your chest.
2. Rotate your torso from the side nearest the pulley to the far side, hands staying in front of your chest.
3. Return slowly and repeat the movement.
Note: The rotation comes from your torso, not from pulling with your arms alone.
exercises.kettlebell-windmill:
1. Stand holding a kettlebell overhead in one hand, the opposite foot turned out.
2. With your eyes up, lower your torso toward that leg while keeping your arm straight overhead.
3. Return to an upright stand while keeping the kettlebell steady overhead.
4. Complete all reps on one side, and switch sides only at the end of the set.
Note: Go slowly and with control; this is an exercise for shoulder stability, not for fast strength.
exercises.kettlebell-halo:
1. Hold a kettlebell upside down (bottom up) close to your chest with both hands.
2. Circle it slowly around your head, in a full circle around your skull.
3. Complete a full circle, then go back in the opposite direction.
Note: Keep your core braced so your torso doesn't sway with the kettlebell.
exercises.kettlebell-row:
1. Get into a bent-over position with a kettlebell in each hand, knees slightly bent.
2. Row both kettlebells to your ribs while squeezing your shoulder blades together.
3. Lower slowly until your arms are fully straight.
Note: Keep your back straight throughout the exercise.
exercises.one-arm-kettlebell-row:
1. Place one hand and one knee on a sturdy bench or chair, with a kettlebell hanging down in the other hand.
2. Row the kettlebell to your ribs while drawing your shoulder blade in.
3. Lower slowly to full extension, and only then repeat the movement.
4. Complete all reps with one hand, and switch hands only at the end of the set.
Note: Keep your back straight and parallel to the floor throughout the set.
exercises.kettlebell-sumo-high-pull:
1. Stand with feet wider than your shoulders, toes turned out, and a kettlebell between your feet.
2. Lift the kettlebell by straightening your hips and knees, and pull it up to chin height, elbows high.
3. Lower slowly between your legs and repeat the movement.
Note: Your elbows lead the movement upward, not your wrists.
exercises.wide-grip-pullup:
1. Grip the bar wider than your shoulders, palms facing forward.
2. Pull your body up until your chin is over the bar.
3. Lower slowly until your arms are fully straight.
Note: A wide grip puts more load on your upper back; don't compromise on full range of motion.
exercises.neutral-grip-pullup:
1. Grip the two handles of the bar with palms facing each other (if your bar has such grips).
2. Pull your body up until your chin is over the bar.
3. Lower slowly until your arms are fully straight.
Note: A neutral grip is easier on the shoulders; a good step before wide-grip pull-ups.
exercises.dumbbell-overhead-carry:
1. Press one dumbbell until your arm is fully straight overhead, the other arm at your side.
2. Walk forward a set distance while keeping your arm straight and steady overhead.
3. Set the dumbbell down, rest, and switch hands for the next walk.
Note: Keep your wrist straight over your shoulder; don't let your arm drift forward or back.
exercises.plyo-pushup:
1. Start in a regular push-up position.
2. Lower down, then push powerfully until your hands leave the floor.
3. Land softly on your hands and flow straight into the next rep.
Note: Keep your core braced on landing to protect your lower back.
exercises.single-arm-pushup:
1. Start in a push-up position with your feet spread wide for stability, one hand behind your back.
2. Lower slowly until your chest almost touches the floor.
3. Push back up with one arm until fully straight.
4. Complete all reps with one arm, and switch arms only at the end of the set.
Note: Spread your feet wider for better stability when you're starting out.
exercises.cable-deadlift:
1. Stand facing the cable machine with a low handle, feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Hinge from the hips to grab the handle, back straight and knees slightly bent.
3. Straighten your hips and knees to an upright stand, then lower back down with control.
Note: The movement is led by pushing the hips back, not by bending your back.
exercises.close-grip-pulldown:
1. Sit at the high pulley machine and grip the narrow handle with both hands.
2. Pull the handle down to upper-chest height, elbows at your sides.
3. Return slowly upward until your arms are almost fully straight.
Note: Lead by driving your elbows back, not by leaning your torso.
exercises.sumo-deadlift:
1. Stand with feet wider than shoulder-width, toes turned slightly out, and the bar over the middle of your feet.
2. Lower down and grip the bar inside your legs, back straight and chest up.
3. Drive through your heels and straighten your hips and knees together to a full stand.
4. Lower the bar back to the floor slowly and with control.
Note: The wide stance shortens the range of motion and shifts more load to your inner thighs.
exercises.barbell-walking-lunge:
1. Rest a bar on your shoulders behind your head, as in a squat.
2. Step forward and lower until your back knee almost touches the floor.
3. Push off your front leg to stand, and step forward with the other leg.
Note: Keep your torso upright throughout the movement so you don't lose your balance.
exercises.barbell-glute-bridge:
1. Sit on the floor with a bar resting on your hips, and lie back until your upper back rests on the floor.
2. Drive through your heels and lift your hips up to a straight line between knees and shoulders.
3. Pause at the top, then lower with control.
Note: Use a pad or towel under the bar to protect your hips.
exercises.zercher-squat:
1. Unrack the bar and hold it in the crook of your elbows, hands clasped underneath.
2. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and squat down while keeping your back straight.
3. Lower until your thighs are parallel to the floor, then drive through your heels back up.
Note: The bar presses on your elbows; start with a very light weight until you get used to the feeling.
exercises.hang-clean:
1. Stand with the bar at mid-thigh height, a shoulder-width grip and a straight back.
2. Drive from your hips and knees in one explosive movement, and shrug your shoulders upward.
3. "Jump" under the bar and catch it on the front of your shoulders in a half-squat.
4. Straighten your hips and knees to a full stand.
Note: This is a technical movement; start with an empty bar and practice the timing before adding weight.
exercises.barbell-rollout:
1. Kneel and hold a light bar in front of you, hands shoulder-width apart.
2. Roll the bar forward while extending your body, keeping your abs braced and back straight.
3. Go as far as is comfortable with control, then pull the bar back to the starting point.
Note: Don't let your lower back sag; if it does, shorten the range.
exercises.barbell-snatch:
1. Stand with the bar over your feet, with a grip wider than shoulder-width.
2. Lift the bar off the floor in one continuous movement, accelerating as the bar passes your knees.
3. At peak acceleration, pull yourself under the bar and catch it overhead with straight arms.
4. Straighten your hips and knees to a full stand with the bar locked out overhead.
Note: An advanced movement that requires good shoulder mobility; learn it with coaching before adding weight.
exercises.barbell-clean-and-jerk:
1. Lift the bar off the floor and catch it on the front of your shoulders with a clean (as in the hang clean).
2. Stand upright with the bar on your shoulders.
3. Bend your knees slightly and drive the bar up in one explosive movement, splitting your legs front and back to catch it.
4. Straighten your arms overhead and return to standing.
Note: An advanced two-part exercise; practice each part separately before combining them.
exercises.barbell-shrug:
1. Stand upright holding a bar in both hands in front of your body, with a shoulder-width grip.
2. Raise your shoulders toward your ears as high as possible, without bending your elbows.
3. Pause briefly at the top, then lower slowly.
Note: The movement comes from the shoulders only; don't help with your arms.
exercises.barbell-box-squat:
1. Place a box of suitable height behind you and unrack the bar onto your shoulders.
2. Lower slowly until you sit lightly on the box, without dropping.
3. Pause briefly on the box, then drive through your heels back to standing.
Note: Don't fully relax on the box; keep tension in your body even at the point of contact.
exercises.incline-bench-press:
1. Lie on an incline bench and unrack the bar with straight arms over your upper chest.
2. Lower the bar slowly until it lightly touches your upper chest.
3. Press the bar back up until your arms are fully straight.
Note: The incline shifts more load to your upper chest and shoulders; keep your shoulder blades pressed into the bench.
exercises.close-grip-bench-press:
1. Lie on a bench and grip the bar at roughly shoulder-width.
2. Lower the bar toward your chest while keeping your elbows close to your body.
3. Press back up to full extension, focusing on using your triceps.
Note: A grip that's too narrow can strain your wrists; keep a comfortable width.
exercises.dumbbell-incline-press:
1. Lie on an incline bench with a dumbbell in each hand at chest level, palms facing forward.
2. Press the dumbbells up until your arms are almost fully straight over your upper chest.
3. Lower slowly back to the starting point.
Note: Don't let the dumbbells "meet" at the top; keep a steady path.
exercises.cable-shoulder-press:
1. Sit facing the cable machine and hold the handles at shoulder height, elbows bent at 90 degrees.
2. Press the handles up until your arms are almost fully straight.
3. Return slowly to the starting point while keeping tension on the cable.
Note: Keep your back straight and don't arch backward while pressing.
exercises.cable-triceps-overhead:
1. Stand with your back to the cable machine and hold the rope with both hands behind your head.
2. Straighten your elbows upward until your arms are almost straight overhead.
3. Return slowly to the starting point while keeping your elbows fixed in place.
Note: Only your forearms move; your upper arms stay steady throughout the movement.
exercises.cable-lateral-raise:
1. Stand between two low cable stations and hold the opposite handle in each hand (right in your left hand and vice versa).
2. Raise your arms out to the sides to shoulder height, with a slight bend in your elbows.
3. Lower slowly back down.
Note: Lead with your elbows, not by shrugging your shoulders.
exercises.kettlebell-clean-and-jerk:
1. Grip the kettlebell and in one movement pull it from the floor to your shoulder (clean).
2. Bend your knees slightly, then drive the kettlebell up with your legs; bend your knees again and drop under the weight to catch it with a straight arm.
3. Straighten your arm overhead and return to standing, then lower the kettlebell with control.
4. Complete all reps with one hand, and switch hands only at the end of the set.
Note: A two-part exercise; practice each part separately before linking them.
exercises.kettlebell-figure-8:
1. Stand with a kettlebell between your legs, a stance slightly wider than shoulder-width, back straight.
2. Pass the kettlebell from one hand, between your legs, to the other hand behind.
3. Continue in a continuous figure-eight between your legs, alternating.
Note: The movement comes from hinging at the hips, not from your lower back.
exercises.double-kettlebell-front-squat:
1. Clean two kettlebells up to your shoulders, elbows high.
2. Squat down while keeping your torso upright and knees pointing out.
3. Drive through your heels back to a full stand.
Note: The weight of the kettlebells in front of your body requires stable abs and torso throughout the movement.
exercises.kettlebell-arnold-press:
1. Lift a kettlebell to one shoulder, palm facing in.
2. Press the kettlebell up while rotating your wrist until your palm faces forward at the top of the movement.
3. Return slowly to the starting point with the reverse rotation.
4. Complete all reps with one hand, and switch hands only at the end of the set.
Note: The rotation adds work for the shoulder; start with a light weight to get used to it.
exercises.kettlebell-jerk:
1. Clean a kettlebell up to one shoulder.
2. Bend your knees slightly and drive the kettlebell up with your legs; bend your knees again to drop under the weight and catch it with a straight arm.
3. Straighten your arm overhead and return to standing, then lower the kettlebell with control.
4. Complete all reps with one hand, and switch hands only at the end of the set.
Note: An advanced movement that requires coordination between your legs and arm; start with a light weight.
exercises.dumbbell-lateral-raise:
1. Stand upright with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
2. Raise your arms out to the sides to shoulder height, with a slight bend in your elbows.
3. Lower slowly back down.
Note: Don't use momentum from your torso to lift the dumbbells.
exercises.incline-dumbbell-curl:
1. Sit on an incline bench with a dumbbell in each hand, arms hanging straight at your sides.
2. Bend your elbows and curl the dumbbells toward your shoulders.
3. Lower slowly back to the starting point.
Note: The incline prevents you from using body momentum; the movement comes from the arm only.
exercises.dumbbell-rear-delt-fly:
1. Lie face down on a slightly inclined bench, with a dumbbell in each hand and arms hanging down.
2. Raise your arms out to the sides to shoulder height, elbows almost straight.
3. Lower slowly back to the starting point.
Note: This exercise builds the rear shoulders and balances out the many pushing exercises in the program.
exercises.hanging-pike:
1. Hang from a pull-up bar with a grip slightly wider than shoulder-width, legs together.
2. Bend your knees to 90 degrees and bring your thighs forward as the starting point.
3. Pull your legs up until your shins come close to the bar.
4. Lower slowly back down without swinging.
Note: An advanced ab exercise; make sure you have full control of hanging leg raises before trying it.
exercises.seated-leg-tucks:
1. Sit on the edge of a chair or bench, legs straight out in front at a slight angle, hands gripping the sides.
2. Lean your torso back slightly as the starting point.
3. Bring your knees toward your body while leaning your torso forward to meet them.
4. Return slowly to the starting point.
Note: A beginner-friendly ab exercise; control the tempo and don't let your legs drop back down.
exercises.knee-tuck-jump:
1. Stand comfortably with knees slightly bent, hands in front of your chest with palms facing down.
2. Dip into a short half-squat and explode up into a jump.
3. In the air, bring your knees to your chest as far as possible, and land with control on bent knees.
Note: Focus on a soft landing; this is an advanced cardio exercise that requires good control of your knee joints.
exercises.double-leg-butt-kick:
1. Stand comfortably with knees slightly bent.
2. Do a short jump up while bending your knees back, as if your heels touch your glutes.
3. Land with control on half-bent knees and repeat the movement.
Note: Fast tempo and small movement; good for warming up and raising your heart rate.
exercises.carioca:
1. Stand with feet slightly apart, arms loose and relaxed.
2. Step sideways by crossing one leg over the other in front, then take a regular step.
3. Repeat with a crossing step behind the next time, alternating, while moving sideways.
Note: Keep your eyes forward and don't turn your feet during the sideways movement.
exercises.rocket-jump:
1. Stand relaxed with feet shoulder-width apart and arms at your sides.
2. Drop into a quick half-squat and explode up into a jump as high as possible.
3. Extend your body in the air with your arms up, and land with control, absorbing through your knees.
Note: Focus on jump height and a soft landing, not on rep speed.
exercises.decline-situp:
1. Set the decline bench to your starting angle and lie on it head down, feet locked under the pad at the top end.
2. Cross your arms over your chest or place your hands behind your head, bend your knees slightly, and lower back with control until your back almost touches the bench.
3. Come back up to a full sitting position by contracting your abs, without pulling on your neck.
Note: The steeper the decline, the harder it is; start moderate and increase gradually.
exercises.glute-bridge-hold:
1. Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor, close to your glutes.
2. Push through your heels and lift your hips until you form a straight line from knees to shoulders.
3. Squeeze your glutes and hold the position without moving, breathing calmly.
Note: If you feel the hold in your lower back rather than your glutes, lower your hips slightly and brace your abs.
exercises.nordic-curl:
1. Kneel on the padding of a dedicated Nordic curl station, and adjust the ankle support according to the station's instructions; make sure the anchor is secure before lowering.
2. Straighten your body into one line from knees to shoulders and brace your abs.
3. Lower forward as slowly as you can control, with the movement coming only from your knees and your hands ready to catch you.
4. Push lightly off your hands and contract your hamstrings to come back up.
Careful: Don't improvise an anchor under a couch or bed; without a suitable station, choose heel slides instead. Start with a partial range, lowering only a third of the way, and go deeper gradually from week to week. As soon as you lose control of the descent, catch yourself with your hands instead of dropping.
exercises.glute-kickback:
1. Get on all fours, hands under your shoulders and knees under your hips.
2. Lift one leg back and up, with the knee staying bent at a right angle and the heel pushing toward the ceiling.
3. Pause for a moment at the top and lower slowly without putting your knee on the floor.
4. Complete all reps on the same leg, and switch legs only at the end of the set.
Note: Stop the lift at the height where your back is still straight; if your lower back arches, you lifted too high.
exercises.side-lying-leg-raise:
1. Lie on your side with your body in one straight line, and rest your head on your lower arm.
2. Place your top hand on the floor in front of you for stability.
3. Raise your straight top leg up to an angle of about 45 degrees, and lower slowly without resting it on the bottom leg.
4. Complete all reps on the same side, and switch sides only at the end of the set.
Note: Point your toes forward, not toward the ceiling; if they turn up, the work shifts from the side of your hip to your hip flexors.
exercises.floor-back-extension:
1. Lie face down with your hands crossed on your chest or beside your head, forehead close to the floor.
2. Brace your abs and squeeze your glutes.
3. Lift your chest off the floor in a smooth movement, with your eyes staying on the floor.
4. Pause for a second at the top and lower slowly back down without dropping.
Note: This is a small-range exercise; lift only as high as is comfortable for your lower back, without arching all the way.
exercises.hamstring-slide:
1. Lie on your back with knees bent, and place a small towel under each heel on a smooth floor (or just wear socks).
2. Push through your heels and lift your hips into a bridge, a straight line from knees to shoulders.
3. Slowly slide your heels forward until your legs are almost straight, without your hips dropping to the floor.
4. Pull your heels back toward you at the same pace, and lower your hips only at the end of the set.
Careful: Do this only on a smooth, clean floor; on a carpet the towel catches midway and your knee stops abruptly.
exercises.wall-sit:
1. Stand with your back against a wall and move your feet about half a meter away from it.
2. Slide your back down the wall until your knees are at a right angle and your thighs are parallel to the floor.
3. Keep your back against the wall and your weight in your heels, and hold the position until the time is up.
Note: Your knees should be directly over your ankles; if they're over your toes, move your feet farther from the wall.
exercises.sumo-squat:
1. Stand with feet wider than your shoulders and toes turned out at a comfortable angle.
2. Lower straight down with your knees opening in the direction your toes point.
3. Go down until your thighs are parallel to the floor or slightly below, with your chest up.
4. Drive through your heels and squeeze your glutes on the way up.
Note: Your knees track the direction of your toes; as soon as they cave inward, shorten the range.
exercises.cossack-squat:
1. Stand with feet much wider than your shoulders and toes turned slightly out.
2. Shift your weight to one leg and squat down on it, with the other leg staying straight on the floor.
3. Reach your arms forward for balance and lower only as deep as is comfortable, without your heel lifting.
4. Push back to the center and lower to the other side, alternating.
Note: The heel of the working leg stays on the floor; if it lifts, widen your stance or go less deep.
exercises.lateral-lunge:
1. Stand upright with feet hip-width apart.
2. Take a wide step to the side and push your hips back, with the other leg staying straight on the floor.
3. Lower until the knee of the stepping leg is over your foot and your chest is up.
4. Push through your heel back to standing and step to the other side, alternating.
Note: The descent comes from pushing your hips back, not from leaning your body over your knee.
exercises.bodyweight-reverse-lunge:
1. Stand upright with feet hip-width apart and hands on your hips.
2. Take a big step back and lower your back knee almost to the floor.
3. Keep your torso upright and your front knee over your foot.
4. Push through your front heel, return to standing and step with the other leg, alternating.
Note: If your balance wobbles, hold lightly onto the back of a sturdy chair until the movement feels steady.
exercises.curtsy-lunge:
1. Stand upright with feet hip-width apart.
2. Step one leg back and diagonally, behind the other leg, like a curtsy.
3. Lower until your back knee is close to the floor, with your hips still facing forward.
4. Push through your front heel back to standing and step with the other leg, alternating.
Note: Don't let your front knee cave inward; push it out toward your little toe.
exercises.shrimp-squat:
1. Stand on one leg, bend the other leg back and hold its ankle with the hand on the same side.
2. Lower slowly on the standing leg until your back knee lightly touches the floor.
3. Keep your chest up and your standing heel on the floor throughout the descent.
4. Drive through your heel and stand back up without putting your back foot on the floor.
5. Complete all reps on the same leg, and switch legs only at the end of the set.
Careful: Place a folded towel under your back knee; hitting a hard floor is the most common injury in this exercise.
exercises.standing-calf-raise:
1. Stand upright with feet hip-width apart, optionally next to a wall with one hand on it for balance.
2. Raise your heels as high as possible and stand on the balls of your feet.
3. Pause for a moment at the top and lower your heels slowly until they touch the floor.
Note: Go up and down slowly; small bounces skip exactly the part that does the work.
exercises.single-leg-calf-raise:
1. Stand on one leg and hold lightly onto a wall or the back of a chair for balance.
2. Bend the other leg back so it doesn't touch the floor.
3. Raise your heel as high as possible, pause for a moment, and lower slowly.
4. Complete all reps on the same leg, and switch legs only at the end of the set.
Note: Your hand on the wall is for balance only; don't lean on it to push yourself up.
exercises.bodyweight-good-morning:
1. Stand with feet hip-width apart and place your hands behind your head, elbows open to the sides.
2. Bend your knees slightly and push your hips back while tipping your torso forward.
3. Lower until your torso is close to parallel with the floor, with a completely straight back and open chest.
4. Drive your hips forward and return to an upright stand.
Note: As soon as your back starts to round, stop there; that's your range for today.
exercises.bodyweight-single-leg-deadlift:
1. Stand on one leg with the knee slightly soft, arms reaching out to the sides for balance.
2. Tip your torso forward while sending your free leg straight back, until you form a straight line from your head to your back heel.
3. Lower until your torso is close to parallel with the floor, with a straight back, and return to standing with control.
4. Complete all reps on the same leg, and switch legs only at the end of the set.
Note: Keep your hips level and square to the floor; don't let the hip of your back leg open out to the side.
exercises.glute-bridge-march:
1. Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor, close to your glutes.
2. Push through your heels and lift your hips into a bridge, a straight line from knees to shoulders.
3. Without lowering your hips, lift one knee toward your chest, return the foot to the floor and lift the other knee, alternating.
4. Finish all the steps and only then lower your hips to the floor.
Note: If your hips drop or rotate as soon as a leg lifts, raise the knee less high and keep the bridge stable.
exercises.bodyweight-bulgarian-split-squat:
1. Stand with your back to a sturdy chair and rest the top of your back foot on it.
2. Place your front foot far enough from the chair that your knee doesn't pass your toes.
3. Lower slowly until your front thigh is almost parallel to the floor, hands in front of you for balance.
4. Push through your front heel and come back up without forcefully locking your knee.
5. Complete all reps on the same leg, and switch legs only at the end of the set.
Note: Push the chair against a wall before the first rep; a chair that slides back pulls your back leg with it.
exercises.chair-pistol-squat:
1. Stand with your back to a sturdy chair, about a foot's length away from it.
2. Stand on one leg and extend the other leg straight forward, arms reaching forward for balance.
3. Lower slowly and with control until your glutes lightly touch the seat, without putting your weight on it.
4. Drive through your heel and stand back up without lowering your free foot to the floor.
5. Complete all reps on the same leg, and switch legs only at the end of the set.
Note: The lower the chair, the harder the exercise; start with a high chair and go lower only once you can stand up without using the seat.
exercises.wide-pushup:
1. Place your hands on the floor wider than your shoulders, about one and a half times shoulder-width, legs straight behind you.
2. Keep a straight line from heels to shoulders and lower your chest to the floor with control.
3. Your elbows flare out at about 60 degrees from your body, not straight out to the sides.
4. Push back up until your arms are fully straight.
Careful: A wide grip loads the front of the shoulder; if you feel tingling or pressure in your shoulder, bring your hands in closer.
exercises.close-grip-pushup:
1. Place your hands on the floor under your chest, close together until your thumbs almost touch.
2. Lower down with your elbows sliding along your body rather than flaring out.
3. Stop when your chest almost touches your hands, keeping your body in one line.
4. Push back up to full extension; you'll feel the work in the back of your arms.
Note: A narrow grip loads your wrists; if they hurt, spread your fingers and widen the gap between your hands slightly.
exercises.clock-pushup:
1. Start in a regular push-up position, hands shoulder-width apart.
2. Do one full push-up.
3. Walk your hands and feet a few centimeters around an imaginary center, like a clock hand moving forward.
4. Do another push-up in the new position, and keep rotating until you've completed a full circle.
Note: While walking, your body stays in a straight line and your hips don't rise; if they rise, take a shorter step.
exercises.pushup-to-side-plank:
1. Start in a regular push-up position and do one push-up.
2. At the end of the push, shift your weight to one hand and rotate your body to the side until you're in a side plank.
3. Raise your free arm straight up and hold for a second with your body locked in one line.
4. Return to the push-up position and do another rep, this time opening to the other side, alternating.
Note: When opening to the side, push the supporting shoulder away from your ear and don't let your hips drop to the floor.
exercises.incline-close-grip-pushup:
1. Place both hands close together on a stable surface at waist height: a table, a windowsill, or the back of a chair braced against a wall.
2. Walk your feet back until your body forms a straight line from heels to shoulders.
3. Bend your elbows and lower your chest to your hands, elbows tucked against your body.
4. Push back up to full extension.
Careful: Make sure the surface doesn't slip or tip before the first rep; press on it with full force while standing, and only then walk back.
exercises.plank-up-down:
1. Start in a forearm plank, elbows under your shoulders and feet hip-width apart.
2. Place one hand where your elbow was and push up, then the other, until you're on straight arms.
3. Lower back to one elbow and then the other, in the same order.
4. Start the next rep with the other hand, so the work is shared equally between both arms.
Note: Spread your feet wide so your hips barely sway from side to side; that's what makes this a shoulder exercise rather than a waist exercise.
exercises.triceps-body-press:
1. Stand facing a stable surface at waist height: a table or the back of a chair braced against a wall.
2. Place both hands on the edge of the surface at shoulder-width and lean forward until your weight is on them.
3. Bend only your elbows and lower your body toward the surface, upper arms tucked against your ribs.
4. Straighten your elbows and push your body back, without pushing off with your legs.
Careful: The surface must be braced against a wall or heavy enough not to move; test it with a firm press before leaning on it.
exercises.drop-pushup:
1. Set up two dedicated plyo platforms that are low, wide and non-slip, at the same height (start at about 5 cm), slightly wider than your shoulders apart, and get into a push-up position with one hand on each.
2. Lift your hands off the platforms and let your body drop to the floor between them.
3. Land on your hands with bent elbows and absorb the drop in a soft, full descent.
4. Push powerfully back up and put your hands back on the platforms.
Careful: Never do this on chairs or on a stack of objects; make sure the platforms can handle the load and don't move. Never land on locked elbows; your arms must go into a bent descent, and if you can't yet do explosive push-ups with full control, don't do this exercise.
exercises.wall-pushup:
1. Stand facing a wall a step away from it and place both hands on the wall at chest height, shoulder-width apart.
2. Keep your body straight from heels to head and bend your elbows until your chest comes close to the wall.
3. Push off with your hands and return to standing with straight arms.
4. The farther your feet are from the wall, the harder the exercise.
Note: Your heels stay on the floor and your hips don't push forward; your body moves as one unit.
exercises.knee-pushup:
1. Get down on your knees and place your hands shoulder-width apart, slightly in front of your chest line.
2. Cross your feet in the air and form a straight line from knees to shoulders.
3. Lower your chest to the floor with control, elbows angled diagonally from your body.
4. Push back up until your arms are fully straight.
Note: Your hips stay in line with your body and don't rise; if it's hard on your knees, put a folded towel under them.
exercises.archer-pushup:
1. Get into a push-up position with your hands much wider than your shoulders.
2. Lower to one side: that arm's elbow bends and your chest goes down over it, while the other arm stays almost straight and slides out to the side.
3. Push back to the center with the bent arm.
4. Do the next rep to the other side, alternating, until you complete the number of reps.
Note: The straight arm supports but isn't forcefully locked; keep a slight bend in the elbow so you don't strain the joint.
exercises.hindu-pushup:
1. Start with hands and feet on the floor and hips high, so your body forms an upside-down V.
2. Bend your elbows and lower your chest in a forward arc, close to the floor, as if passing under a low bar.
3. Continue the movement forward and up until your arms are straight, chest open and hips close to the floor.
4. Lift your hips and bring your body back in the reverse movement to the starting position.
Careful: Move into the arch slowly; don't drop your lower back, and if you feel pressure in your back, don't lift your chest high.
exercises.spiderman-pushup:
1. Start in a push-up position with hands shoulder-width apart.
2. As you lower, draw one knee out toward the elbow on the same side, the leg staying off the floor.
3. At the bottom, return the leg to its place and push back up.
4. On the next rep, draw the other knee, alternating.
Note: Your hips stay parallel to the floor; don't let them tilt to the side to bring the knee higher.
exercises.sphinx-pushup:
1. Start in a forearm plank, elbows under your shoulders, palms flat on the floor.
2. Straighten your elbows and push your body up until you're on your palms, without moving your hands and without lifting your hips.
3. Your body rises and lowers as one rigid unit, like a board.
4. Lower slowly back until your forearms touch the floor again.
Note: The entire movement is at the elbow only; if your hips rise or your hands slide forward, drop your knees to the floor and start with an easier version.
exercises.pseudo-planche-pushup:
1. Get into a push-up position and move your hands back until they're at waist level, fingers turned slightly out.
2. Lean your shoulders forward so they're in front of the line of your hands.
3. Lower down while keeping the forward lean and your elbows tucked against your ribs.
4. Push back up without letting your shoulders shift back.
Note: Your wrists work hard in this position; warm them up first, and turn your hands slightly outward or support yourself on your fists if there's pain.
exercises.wall-handstand-hold:
1. Stand facing a clear wall, bend down and place your hands on the floor close to it, shoulder-width apart.
2. Only if you already have control of getting into and out of a handstand: shift your weight onto your hands and kick up one leg with a small swing, followed by the other, until your heels rest gently against the wall with your back facing it.
3. Push hard through your shoulders toward the floor, brace your abs and glutes, and look between your hands.
4. Hold as long as you have full control, then lower one leg at a time back to the floor.
Careful: Don't wait until you're completely exhausted; come down just before your control runs out, one leg at a time, and clear the floor around you of furniture and objects beforehand.
exercises.wall-walk:
1. Lie face down with your feet against the wall and your hands on the floor under your shoulders.
2. Push up with your hands and walk one foot after the other up the wall, while at the same time walking your hands toward the wall.
3. Keep walking until your chest is close to the wall and your body is almost vertical.
4. Come down exactly the same way: walk your hands back and your feet down, slowly and with control, until you're lying down.
Careful: The descent is the dangerous part; don't fall back and don't let your lower back arch. If you feel you're losing control, come down immediately, one foot at a time.
exercises.elevated-pike-pushup:
1. Place your feet on a sturdy chair and your hands on the floor at shoulder-width.
2. Walk your hands toward the chair until your hips are high and your body is almost vertical.
3. Bend your elbows and slowly lower the top of your head toward the floor, slightly in front of your hands.
4. Push back up until your arms are fully straight.
Careful: Make sure the chair is against a wall and doesn't slide back, and lower only to a depth you can push back up from.
exercises.prone-y-raise:
1. Lie face down with your forehead close to the floor and your arms stretched forward diagonally, like the letter Y, thumbs up.
2. Lift both arms off the floor without bending your elbows, to the height where you're still in control.
3. Hold for a second at the top and feel your shoulder blades come together and move down toward your hips.
4. Lower slowly back to the floor.
Note: Your shoulders don't rise toward your ears; if they do, lift less high. Your neck stays relaxed and your eyes on the floor.
exercises.prone-t-raise:
1. Lie face down with your forehead close to the floor and your arms straight out to the sides, like the letter T, thumbs up.
2. Lift both arms off the floor in a smooth movement, arms staying straight.
3. Squeeze your shoulder blades together and hold for a second at the top.
4. Lower slowly back to the floor and only then start the next rep.
Note: Don't lift your chest off the floor to get higher; only your arms rise, and your lower back stays relaxed.
exercises.superman-pull:
1. Lie face down with your arms stretched forward and your feet on the floor.
2. Lift your arms and chest slightly off the floor.
3. Pull both elbows back toward your ribs, as if pulling something toward you, and squeeze your shoulder blades together.
4. Reach your arms back forward with control, without resting them on the floor between reps.
Note: Your chest rises only a little; the goal is a shoulder-blade pull, not arching your lower back.
exercises.crunch:
1. Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor; unlike a full sit-up, here your lower back stays on the floor the whole time.
2. Place your hands lightly beside your head, elbows pointing out.
3. Curl your shoulders just a few centimeters off the floor, and pause for a second at the top.
4. Lower slowly back until your shoulders touch the floor.
Note: Your hands only support your head; if you feel a pull in your neck, cross them over your chest instead.
exercises.bent-knee-hip-raise:
1. Lie on your back with your arms at your sides, palms down; they stabilize you throughout the exercise.
2. Bend your knees at a fixed angle and lift your feet a few centimeters off the floor.
3. Pull your knees toward your chest until your hips curl slightly off the floor, without changing the knee angle.
4. Lower slowly back down without setting your feet down.
Note: The lift comes from curling your hips, not from momentum; if you're "throwing" your legs, slow down the tempo.
exercises.v-up:
1. Lie on your back with legs straight and arms stretched overhead, your body stretched out in one line.
2. Lift your straight legs and upper body at the same time, so your hands and feet meet above your belly and your body forms a V shape.
3. Lower slowly back to the straight line, without dropping your heels and hands forcefully.
Note: If your lower back lifts off the floor on the way down, bend your knees slightly and shorten the range of motion.
exercises.side-jackknife:
1. Lie on one side with your legs straight and stacked; your bottom arm rests on your belly and your top hand is beside your head.
2. Lift both legs and your upper body toward the same side at the same time, so your top elbow comes toward your thigh.
3. Pause for a second in the squeeze and lower slowly back down.
4. Do all reps on one side, then switch sides.
Note: The movement is a side bend only; don't rotate your chest toward the floor or the ceiling.
exercises.oblique-crunch:
1. Lie on one side with knees slightly bent, one leg on top of the other; here your lower body stays on the floor and only your chest rises.
2. Place your top hand behind your head and your bottom hand on the floor for stability.
3. Lift your top elbow and chest upward until you feel a squeeze in the side of your abs, and pause for a second.
4. Lower slowly back down. Do all reps on one side, then switch sides.
Note: Don't pull your head with your hand; your neck stays in line with your spine.
exercises.cross-body-crunch:
1. Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor, hands lightly behind your head.
2. Lift your right shoulder toward your left knee, while at the same time bringing your left knee toward your shoulder; the shoulder moves, not just the elbow.
3. Return to the starting position and repeat the movement with your left shoulder and right knee, alternating.
Note: The shoulder leads; if only your elbow moves toward your knee, your abs aren't working.
exercises.heel-touch:
1. Lie on your back with knees bent, feet on the floor about half a meter apart, arms straight at your sides.
2. Lift your shoulders slightly off the floor and stay that way throughout the set; this is a small side-to-side movement, not a crunch.
