3. Bend your torso to the right and touch your right heel with your fingertips, then to the left and your left heel, alternating.
Note: Your shoulders don't rest between sides; if they drop, cut the set short rather than giving up the position.
exercises.frog-situp:
1. Lie on your back, bend your knees and let them fall out to the sides until the soles of your feet touch and your legs form a diamond shape.
2. Draw your feet as close to your hips as is comfortable, and cross your arms over your chest.
3. Raise your upper body about a quarter of the way to sitting, pause for a second, and lower slowly.
Note: Opening the knees takes the hip flexors out of the movement, so the range is short on purpose; don't try to reach a full sit-up.
exercises.cocoon:
1. Lie on your back with legs straight and arms stretched overhead.
2. Draw your knees to your chest and curl your hips slightly off the floor, while at the same time bringing your arms over your head and forward; your body curls into a ball.
3. Pause for a moment when everything is tucked, then slowly open back out to a straight line.
Note: Your head and arms move together with your knees; if your arms get ahead, that's momentum, not ab work.
exercises.plank-pike:
1. Set up in a plank on your forearms and toes, elbows under your shoulders; this is a moving version of the plank, not a hold.
2. Push your hips up toward the ceiling until your body forms an upside-down V, and draw your ribs toward your hips.
3. Lower slowly back to a straight plank line without your hips sagging.
Note: Your heels stay on the floor as much as possible; if your hamstrings are tight, bend your knees slightly.
exercises.spider-crawl:
1. Set up in a push-up position and lower yourself until your elbows are bent at about ninety degrees; the whole exercise is done in this low position, and that's what makes it unique.
2. Lift one foot, open the knee out to the side and bring it forward toward the elbow on the same side.
3. Return the leg to its place and switch legs, alternating.
Note: If you can't hold the low position with a straight back, do the same movement from straight arms; a smaller range is better than sagging hips.
exercises.bird-dog:
1. Get on all fours: hands under your shoulders and knees under your hips, back flat like a table.
2. Reach one arm forward and at the same time the opposite leg back, until they're at back height, no higher.
3. Pause for two seconds, return to the starting position and alternate sides.
Note: Your hips don't rotate; imagine a glass of water on your lower back that mustn't spill.
exercises.hollow-rock:
1. Lie on your back, press your lower back into the floor and lift your shoulders and legs into a hollow hold, arms stretched overhead.
2. Start rocking your whole body back and forth like a rocking chair; the rocking comes from your chest and shoulders.
3. Keep the banana shape completely fixed throughout the rocking.
Note: As soon as the shape opens and your lower back lifts, stop; that's the sign the set is over.
exercises.plank-shoulder-tap:
1. Set up in a plank on straight arms, hands under your shoulders and feet hip-width apart.
2. Lift one hand and touch the opposite shoulder, then return it to the floor and switch hands, alternating.
3. Keep your hips completely still; the whole exercise is about not letting your hips sway while one hand is in the air.
Note: The wider apart your feet, the easier it is to stabilize; spread them if your hips sway.
exercises.plank-jack:
1. Set up in a plank on your forearms or on straight arms, feet together.
2. Jump both feet out wide, and immediately jump them back in; your upper body doesn't move at all.
3. Keep a steady pace; each out-and-in counts as one rep.
Note: If you're at home with neighbors below, step one foot at a time out and in instead of jumping; the work is the same and the noise disappears.
exercises.side-plank-hip-dip:
1. Set up in a side plank on one forearm, elbow directly under your shoulder, body in a straight line.
2. Slowly lower your hips toward the floor without touching it; here, unlike a regular side plank, your hips move.
3. Push your hips back up to a straight line and even slightly beyond.
4. Do all reps on one side, then switch sides.
Note: Your supporting shoulder stays away from your ear; push the floor away from you and don't let your shoulder sink.
exercises.reverse-plank:
1. Sit on the floor with your legs straight in front of you and your palms on the floor behind your hips, fingers pointing toward your feet.
2. Push through your hands and heels and lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to heels, face up.
3. Hold the position with your glutes squeezed and chest open; this is the only hold here that works the whole back side of your body.
Note: If your wrists are sensitive, do the hold on your forearms instead of your hands.
exercises.copenhagen-plank:
1. Lie on your side next to a sturdy chair or bench, and place your top leg on it, with the inside of your ankle or shin resting on the surface.
2. Prop yourself up on your bottom forearm, elbow under your shoulder.
3. Lift your hips and bottom leg off the floor until your body forms a straight line, and press your top leg into the surface; all your weight hangs on your inner-thigh muscle.
4. Hold, then switch sides.
Careful: Start with your top knee bent and your whole shin on the surface (shorter and easier), and only when that's stable move to a straight leg with your ankle at the edge. Make sure the chair doesn't slide on the floor, and sharp pain in your inner thigh means stop immediately.
exercises.bear-plank-hold:
1. Get on all fours: hands under your shoulders, knees under your hips and bent at a right angle.
2. Press your toes into the floor and lift your knees only about three centimeters; they hover and don't rise high.
3. Hold the position with a flat back; the lower your knees, the more your abs work.
Note: Your back stays flat like a table; if your hips rise into the air, that's a different position and your abs stop working.
exercises.lying-windshield-wiper:
1. Lie on your back and spread your arms out to the sides in a T shape; they're the anchor that keeps your shoulders from lifting.
2. Raise your straight legs until they point straight up at the ceiling.
3. Lower both legs together to one side as far as you can control, without the opposite shoulder leaving the floor.
4. Bring them back to the center with control and continue to the other side, alternating.
Note: If your lower back is strained or your shoulder lifts, bend your knees to ninety degrees and reduce the range of rotation.
exercises.sit-through:
1. Start in a bear plank: hands under your shoulders and knees hovering above the floor.
2. Lift one hand and kick the opposite leg under your body to the open side, opening your hips toward the ceiling, until you're almost sitting on your side.
3. Bring your leg and hand back to the bear plank and alternate sides.
Careful: The hand that stays on the floor carries all your weight during the transition; start very slowly, and in particular make sure the floor isn't slippery and your knee doesn't drag on it.
exercises.toe-touch-crunch:
1. Lie on your back and raise your straight legs until they point straight up at the ceiling; your legs stay there and don't move throughout the set, and that's the difference from a V-up.
2. Reach your hands up toward your toes and lift your shoulders off the floor until your fingertips come close to your feet.
3. Lower slowly back until your shoulders touch the floor.
Note: If you can't reach your toes, don't pull your head forward; bend your knees slightly and reach for your shins.
exercises.cross-body-mountain-climber:
1. Set up in a push-up position with arms straight under your shoulders.
2. Drive one knee toward the opposite elbow; this rotation is the difference from a regular mountain climber, where the knee travels straight forward.
3. Return the leg back and switch legs continuously, like running in place on a diagonal.
Note: Your hips stay low and parallel to the floor; if your glutes rise into the air, slow down until the movement is controlled.
exercises.band-reverse-fly:
1. Stand on the middle of the band with both feet and hold one end in each hand, hands crossed below your chest.
2. Hinge your torso forward from the hips to about 45 degrees, back straight and chest open.
3. Open your arms out to the sides to shoulder height, drawing your shoulder blades together.
4. Return slowly inward without releasing the tension in the band.
Note: Your arms are almost straight and the movement comes from your shoulder blades; don't bend your elbows and pull like a row.
exercises.band-pull-through:
1. Anchor the band low behind you: around the leg of a heavy table, or with a dedicated anchor at the bottom of a door.
2. Stand with your back to the anchor, pass the band between your legs and hold it with both hands, then step forward until it's taut.
3. Push your hips back and tip your torso forward with a straight back; your hands are pulled back between your legs.
4. Drive your hips forward and return to an upright stand while squeezing your glutes, without pulling with your arms.
Careful: Make sure the anchor doesn't move and the band isn't worn; it stretches right between your legs and must not snap back.
exercises.band-hip-adduction:
1. Anchor the band low to your side (around the leg of a heavy table or with a dedicated anchor at the bottom of a door) and slip the ankle nearest the anchor into the loop.
2. Stand upright at a distance where the band is already taut, and use a wall or the back of a chair for balance.
3. Pull your inner leg across your body toward the far side, until it slightly crosses your standing leg.
4. Return the leg slowly to the starting point. Do all reps on one side, then switch sides.
Careful: Make sure the anchor doesn't move and the band isn't worn, and keep your hips facing forward; don't rotate your body to move the leg farther.
exercises.band-skull-crusher:
1. Anchor the band low (around the leg of a heavy table or with a dedicated anchor at the bottom of a door) and lie on your back with your head toward the anchor.
2. Hold one end in each hand and raise your arms straight over your chest, elbows pointing in.
3. Bend only your elbows and lower your hands toward your forehead, until your forearms almost touch the band.
4. Straighten your elbows back up over your chest.
Careful: Make sure the anchor doesn't move and the band isn't worn; it stretches over your face, and an end that snaps free goes straight to your head.
exercises.band-calf-raise:
1. Stand on the middle of the band with the balls of your feet, feet hip-width apart.
2. Hold one end in each hand and pull it up to shoulder height, so the band is stretched upward.
3. Raise your heels as high as possible and pause for a moment at the top.
4. Lower your heels slowly to the floor, without dropping.
Note: The band must sit under the balls of your feet, not your toes; from there it slips forward as you rise.
exercises.band-crossover:
1. Anchor the band behind you at shoulder height: around the leg of a heavy table, or with a dedicated anchor in the middle of a door.
2. Hold one end in each hand, step forward until the band is taut, and place one foot in front for stability.
3. Open your arms out to the sides at chest height with a slight bend in your elbows.
4. Bring both hands forward and in until they cross in front of the center of your chest, then open slowly.
Careful: Make sure the anchor doesn't move and the band isn't worn; you're standing with your back to it, and an end that snaps free goes straight to your back.
exercises.band-external-rotation:
1. Anchor the band at elbow height: around the leg of a heavy table, or with a dedicated anchor in the middle of a door.
2. Stand side-on to the anchor, and hold the end in the hand farther from it.
3. Tuck your elbow against your side, bent at 90 degrees, with your forearm across your belly.
4. Rotate your forearm outward until it points forward, and return slowly inward. Do all reps with one arm, then switch arms.
Careful: Make sure the anchor doesn't move and the band isn't worn, and keep your elbow glued to your body; if it drifts away, your shoulder stops working.
exercises.band-internal-rotation:
1. Anchor the band at elbow height: around the leg of a heavy table, or with a dedicated anchor in the middle of a door.
2. Stand side-on to the anchor, and hold the end in the hand nearer to it.
3. Tuck your elbow against your side, bent at 90 degrees, with your forearm pointing out away from your body.
4. Rotate your forearm inward across your belly, and return slowly outward with control. Do all reps with one arm, then switch arms.
Careful: Make sure the anchor doesn't move and the band isn't worn, and use light resistance; this is a shoulder control exercise, not a strength exercise.
exercises.band-hip-extension:
1. Anchor the band low in front of you (around the leg of a heavy table, or with a dedicated anchor at the bottom of a door) and slip one ankle into the loop.
2. Stand facing the anchor at a distance where the band is already taut, and hold the back of a chair or a wall for balance.
3. Kick your leg back in a straight line, squeezing your glutes, as far as you can without arching your back.
4. Return the leg slowly forward. Do all reps on one leg, then switch legs.
Careful: Make sure the anchor doesn't move and the band isn't worn, and keep your torso upright; your glutes push the leg, not your lower back.
exercises.band-hip-flexion:
1. Anchor the band low behind you (around the leg of a heavy table, or with a dedicated anchor at the bottom of a door) and slip one ankle into the loop.
2. Stand with your back to the anchor, at a distance where the band is already taut, and hold a wall or the back of a chair for balance.
3. Raise your knee forward and up until your thigh is parallel to the floor.
4. Lower the leg slowly without letting the band pull it back. Do all reps on one leg, then switch legs.
Careful: Make sure the anchor doesn't move and the band isn't worn, and keep your torso upright; don't lean back to lift your knee higher.
exercises.band-hip-lift:
1. Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor, close to your glutes.
2. Place the middle of the band across your hip bones, and pin one end to the floor under each hand; your hands are the anchor.
3. Push through your heels and lift your hips until you form a straight line from knees to shoulders, against the band's tension.
4. Squeeze your glutes at the top for a moment and lower slowly back down.
Careful: Place the band on the bone, not the soft belly, and make sure your hands hold it firmly to the floor before you lift.
exercises.band-lateral-raise:
1. Stand on the middle of the band with both feet and hold one end in each hand beside your thighs.
2. Raise your arms out to the sides to shoulder height, with a slight bend in your elbows.
3. Lower slowly back down without fully releasing the tension.
Note: Lead with your elbows and stop at shoulder height; don't shrug your shoulders toward your ears.
exercises.band-overhead-triceps-extension:
1. Stand on one end of the band with one foot, or anchor it low around the leg of a heavy table behind you.
2. Hold the other end with both hands and bring it behind your head, elbows bent and pointing up.
3. Straighten your elbows and push your hands up until your arms are almost straight overhead.
4. Return slowly behind your head without your elbows moving forward or out to the sides.
Careful: Make sure the anchor doesn't move and the band isn't worn; it runs behind your head, and an end that snaps free hits the back of your neck.
exercises.band-hamstring-curl:
1. Anchor the band low in front of you: around the leg of a heavy table, or with a dedicated anchor at the bottom of a door.
2. Sit on the floor facing the anchor with legs straight, and slip both ankles into the loop.
3. Move back until the band is taut, and support yourself with your hands on the floor behind your back.
4. Bend your knees and pull your heels toward your glutes, then slowly straighten your legs back out.
Careful: Make sure the anchor doesn't move and the band isn't worn; if it snaps free, your legs shoot forward all at once.
exercises.band-row:
1. Sit on the floor with your legs straight in front of you, and loop the middle of the band around your feet.
2. Hold one end in each hand, straighten your back and lean back slightly until the band is already taut.
3. Pull both hands to your belly, elbows close to your body and shoulder blades coming together.
4. Return your hands forward slowly until fully extended, without rounding your back.
Careful: The band must sit on the soles of your feet, not your toes, and make sure it isn't worn; it stretches right in front of your face.
exercises.band-lat-pulldown:
1. Anchor the band high: with a dedicated anchor at the top of a door, or around a sturdy pull-up bar.
2. Kneel on one or both knees under the anchor, and hold one end in each hand with your arms straight up and wider than your shoulders.
3. Pull both hands down to upper-chest height, drawing your shoulder blades down and flaring your elbows out to the sides.
4. Return your hands up slowly to full extension, without the band pulling you off the floor.
Careful: Make sure the anchor doesn't move and the band isn't worn; it stretches above your head, and an end that snaps free goes straight to your face.
exercises.band-face-pull:
1. Anchor the band at face height: with a dedicated anchor in the middle of a door, or around a sturdy post or railing at face height.
2. Hold one end in each hand with an overhand grip, and step back until your arms are straight and the band is taut.
3. Pull the band toward your face while flaring your elbows out to the sides at shoulder height, until your hands are on either side of your head.
4. Return forward slowly with full control.
Careful: Make sure the anchor doesn't move and the band isn't worn; it stretches right in front of your face. Use light resistance and keep your shoulders down.
exercises.band-biceps-curl:
1. Stand on the middle of the band with both feet, feet hip-width apart.
2. Hold one end in each hand with an underhand grip (palms facing up), arms straight beside your thighs.
3. Bend your elbows and raise your hands to chest height, elbows tucked against your body.
4. Lower slowly to full extension without releasing the tension.
Note: Your body stays upright; don't swing your back for help, and make sure your feet cover the full width of the band so it doesn't slip out.
exercises.band-deadlift:
1. Stand on the middle of the band with both feet, feet hip-width apart; your feet are the anchor.
2. Push your hips back, lower with a straight back, and grab one end in each hand beside your knees.
3. Push the floor away with your legs and rise to a full stand, with your arms straight and the band stretching along your legs.
4. Push your hips back and lower slowly along the same path.
Careful: Don't round your lower back, and make sure the band sits under the middle of your foot and not under your heel; from there it slips out as you rise.
exercises.band-pallof-press:
1. Anchor the band at chest height: with a dedicated anchor in the middle of a door, or around the leg of a heavy table.
2. Stand side-on to the anchor, hold the end with both hands against your chest, and step sideways until the band is taut.
3. Press your hands straight out in front of the center of your chest, without your torso rotating toward the anchor.
4. Hold for a second or two and bring your hands back to your chest with control. Do all reps on one side, then switch sides.
Careful: Make sure the anchor doesn't move and the band isn't worn. The band tries to rotate you; the job is to stay completely stable.
exercises.band-woodchop:
1. Anchor the band high: with a dedicated anchor at the top of a door, or around a sturdy pull-up bar.
2. Stand side-on to the anchor, feet shoulder-width apart, and hold the end with both hands above the shoulder nearest the anchor.
3. Pull diagonally across your body, from high up to outside your far hip, while rotating your torso and hips together.
4. Return slowly to the starting point without the band dragging you. Do all reps on one side, then switch sides.
Careful: Make sure the anchor doesn't move and the band isn't worn; it passes over your shoulder next to your face throughout each rep.
exercises.band-thruster:
1. Stand on the middle of the band with both feet, feet shoulder-width apart; your feet are the anchor.
2. Hold one end in each hand at shoulder height, palms facing in.
3. Squat down fully while your hands stay at your shoulders and the band stays taut.
4. Stand up with momentum, and in the same single movement press your hands straight overhead.
5. Lower your hands back to your shoulders and start a new rep.
Note: The band's tension is greatest right at the end of the press; keep your elbows steady there, and don't let the band snap your hands back down.
exercises.strap-biceps-curl:
1. Hold the strap handles in both hands, palms facing up, facing the anchor point.
2. Walk your feet forward and lean back until your body is at a diagonal, arms straight.
3. Bend your elbows and pull your body up until your fists reach the sides of your forehead, elbows high and fixed in place.
4. Return slowly until your arms are fully straight. Walk your feet forward to make it harder, back to make it easier.
Careful: Make sure the straps are locked to a high, stable anchor point and pull on them hard with both hands before the first rep. Your body stays in a locked straight line from shoulders to heels, without bending at the hips.
exercises.strap-triceps-extension:
1. Hold the strap handles, turn your back to the anchor point and lean forward with your arms straight in front of you.
2. Bend only your elbows and lower your head forward and down until your hands are beside your face, elbows high and pointing forward.
3. Straighten your elbows and push your body back up to straight arms.
4. Walk your feet back to make it harder, forward to make it easier.
Careful: Make sure the straps are locked to a high anchor point; test them with a hard pull before you lean on them. Your body stays in a locked straight line from shoulders to heels and only your forearms move.
exercises.strap-chest-fly:
1. Hold the strap handles, turn your back to the anchor point and lean forward with your arms straight in front of your chest.
2. Open your arms out to the sides in a wide arc, elbows slightly bent and fixed, until you feel a stretch in your chest.
3. Bring your hands together and return to the starting point without bending your elbows.
4. Walk your feet back to make it harder, forward to make it easier; start from a comfortable angle.
Careful: Make sure the straps are locked to a high, stable anchor point and test them with a pull before the exercise. Your body stays in a locked straight line from shoulders to heels so your lower back doesn't sag as you open.
exercises.strap-y-fly:
1. Hold the strap handles, facing the anchor point, and walk your feet forward until your body leans back at a diagonal.
2. Start with your arms straight in front of your chest and your abs braced.
3. Raise your straight arms up and out until they form a letter Y overhead, and let your body follow them up.
4. Return slowly to the starting position. Walk your feet forward to make it harder, back to make it easier.
Careful: Make sure the straps are locked to a high anchor point and test them with a pull before the exercise. Your body stays in a locked straight line from shoulders to heels and your shoulders don't rise to your ears.
exercises.strap-face-pull:
1. Hold the strap handles, facing the anchor point, and walk your feet forward until your body leans back at a diagonal, arms straight.
2. Pull the handles to face height while flaring your elbows out to the sides and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
3. Pause briefly when your hands are on either side of your head, then return slowly to full extension.
4. Walk your feet forward to make it harder, back to make it easier.
Careful: Make sure the straps are locked to a high, stable anchor point and pull on them hard before you lean back. Your body stays in a locked straight line from shoulders to heels throughout the pull.
exercises.strap-pike:
1. Place your feet in the strap handles and get into a plank on your hands, hands under your shoulders.
2. Lift your hips and push them toward the ceiling with straight legs, until your body forms an upside-down V.
3. Lower your hips slowly back to a straight line, without letting your lower back sag.
4. To make it easier, lower the straps so your feet are close to the floor; to make it harder, raise them.
Careful: Make sure the straps are locked to a stable anchor point and test them with a pull before putting your feet in. Between reps your body is locked in one straight line and your hips don't sag.
exercises.strap-atomic-pushup:
1. Place your feet in the strap handles and get into a push-up position on your hands.
2. Do one full push-up: lower your chest with control and push back up until your arms are straight.
3. Right after, pull both knees to your chest, and return your legs to a straight line. That's one rep.
4. To make it easier, lower the straps so your feet are close to the floor, or for now do only one of the two parts; to make it harder, raise them.
Careful: Make sure the straps are locked to a high, stable anchor point and pull on them before the first rep. Your body stays locked in a straight line in the transition between the two parts, without throwing your hips up.
exercises.strap-reverse-lunge:
1. Stand facing the anchor point and hold the strap handles in both hands, elbows slightly bent and body upright.
2. Step back with one leg and lower your back knee almost to the floor.
3. Push through the heel of your front leg and return to standing, with the straps helping only with balance.
4. Do all reps on one leg, then switch legs. To make it easier, pull a bit more with your arms; to make it harder, hold on only lightly.
Careful: Make sure the straps are locked to a stable anchor point and test them with a pull before the exercise. Your torso stays upright and locked in one line with your back thigh, without hanging your body weight on your arms.
exercises.strap-mountain-climber:
1. Place your feet in the strap handles and get into a push-up position on your hands, hands under your shoulders.
2. Pull one knee to your chest without lifting your hips.
3. Return it back and switch legs at a continuous pace, like running in place.
4. To make it easier, lower the straps so your feet are close to the floor and slow the pace; to make it harder, raise them.
Careful: Make sure the straps are locked to a stable anchor point and test them with a pull before putting your feet in. Your body stays locked in a straight line from shoulders to heels and your hips don't bob up and down with the pace.
exercises.strap-plank:
1. Place your feet in the strap handles and get down into a forearm plank, elbows under your shoulders.
2. Lift your body into a straight line from shoulders to heels and brace your abs.
3. Hold the position without moving and breathe calmly, even when the straps try to move your legs.
4. To make it easier, lower the straps so your feet are close to the floor; to make it harder, raise them.
Careful: Make sure the straps are locked to a stable anchor point and test them with a pull before putting your feet in. Your body is locked in a straight line and your hips don't sag, even when the straps sway.
exercises.strap-single-arm-row:
1. Hold one strap handle in one hand, facing the anchor point, with your other arm against your body.
2. Walk your feet forward and lean back until your body is at a diagonal and your arm is straight.
3. Pull your body up to your hand while drawing your shoulder blade in, without rotating your hips or shoulders.
4. Return slowly to full extension. Do all reps with one arm, then switch arms. Step forward to make it harder, back to make it easier.
Careful: Make sure the straps are locked to a high, stable anchor point and pull hard before the first rep. Your body stays in a locked straight line and your chest faces forward throughout the pull.
exercises.diagonal-bound:
1. Stand comfortably, one foot slightly forward and knees soft.
2. Push off your front leg diagonally forward and to the side, driving the opposite knee up.
3. Land on the other leg and absorb the landing with a bent knee.
4. Keep alternating from diagonal to diagonal, crossing an imaginary line on the floor with each bound.
Note: Keep your knee lined up over your toes when landing, without letting it collapse inward.
exercises.side-long-jump:
1. Stand with feet hip-width apart, chest up and knees and hips slightly bent.
2. Lean your body toward the side you're jumping to and swing your arms in the same direction.
3. Jump sideways as far as you can control, and land on both feet facing the same direction.
4. Absorb the landing through your ankles and knees, stabilize fully, and only then jump to the other side.
Careful: Clear about two meters to each side before you start; don't jump for distance toward furniture or a wall.
exercises.single-leg-hop:
1. Stand on one leg with the knee slightly bent, and lift the knee of the other leg.
2. Dip slightly on the supporting knee and hop forward over an imaginary line on the floor.
3. Land on the same leg with a soft knee, stabilize, and continue to the next hop.
4. Do all reps on one leg, then switch sides.
Note: Your knee must stay over your foot when landing; if it caves inward, shorten the hop.
exercises.single-leg-lateral-hop:
1. Stand on one leg beside an imaginary line on the floor, knee slightly bent.
2. Dip slightly at the knee and hop sideways over the line, landing on the same leg.
3. As soon as you land, hop back to the starting side, and keep going back and forth at a steady pace.
4. Do all reps on one leg, then switch sides.
Note: Land softly on the ball of your foot with your knee over your toes, and don't straighten your knee when landing.
exercises.single-leg-push-off:
1. Choose a low, wide, non-slip training platform designed for landings; don't do this on a household chair.
2. Stand facing it and place one whole foot in the middle of the platform.
3. Push hard off the leg on the platform, rise into the air and land with the same foot back on the platform.
4. Do all reps on one leg, then switch sides.
Careful: Make sure the platform is stable and doesn't slip, and start with a low push-off until your landing on the platform is precise.
exercises.forward-hops:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and imagine a row of lines on the floor in front of you, a small step apart.
2. Bend your knees slightly and swing both arms to hop forward over the first line.
3. Land on both feet, absorb through your knees, and immediately hop to the next line.
4. Keep going continuously over the distance you've cleared.
Note: Land with bent knees; a chain of hops on locked knees strains your ankles and lower back.
exercises.lateral-hops:
1. Stand with feet hip-width apart, facing one fixed direction with an imaginary line beside you.
2. Bend your knees slightly and hop sideways over the line, with both feet together.
3. Land softly and immediately hop back to the other side, in a steady rhythm.
Note: Stay on the balls of your feet with soft knees on every landing, and keep facing the same direction.
exercises.high-knees:
1. Stand upright with elbows bent at a right angle.
2. Raise one knee to hip height and quickly switch to the other knee, in place.
3. Stay on the balls of your feet and pump your arms in time with your legs.
4. Keep a steady pace for the whole set time.
Note: Bring your knee up to your body rather than leaning your back backward to get higher.
exercises.running-in-place:
1. Stand upright with feet hip-width apart and elbows bent at your sides.
2. Run in place with small, quick steps, with your knees coming up only a little.
3. Land on the balls of your feet and swing your arms forward and back in rhythm with your legs.
Note: Keep a pace at which you can still talk; this is a tool for warming up and raising your heart rate, not a sprint.
exercises.step-jack:
1. Stand upright with feet together and arms at your sides.
2. Step one foot out to the side while raising both arms overhead.
3. Return your foot and arms to the starting position, and alternate legs.
4. Keep a continuous pace throughout the set.
Note: Your foot is placed on the floor with a step, not a jump; this is the quiet version for a home with neighbors below or for sensitive knees.
exercises.lateral-shuffle:
1. Stand in a half-squat, chest up and eyes forward.
2. Shuffle quickly sideways two or three small steps, without your feet crossing.
3. Stop and change direction back to the starting point.
4. Keep going back and forth for the whole set time.
Careful: Clear about two meters to each side and make sure the floor isn't slippery; in socks on a wooden floor this exercise is dangerous.
exercises.bear-crawl:
1. Get down on all fours, hands under your shoulders and knees under your hips.
2. Lift your knees about two finger-widths off the floor and keep your back straight.
3. Move forward with opposite limbs, right hand with left foot, in small steps.
4. After a few steps, move backward the same way, going back and forth in the space you've cleared.
Note: Keep your hips low and stable; if your glutes rise or your body sways side to side, take shorter steps.
exercises.crab-walk:
1. Sit on the floor with knees bent and your palms behind you, fingers pointing toward your feet.
2. Lift your hips off the floor until your torso is almost parallel to the floor.
3. Move forward or backward in small steps with opposite hand and foot, without lowering your hips.
4. After a few steps, change direction and return to the starting point.
Note: Keep your shoulders away from your ears, and if you feel pressure in your wrists, turn your hands slightly outward.
exercises.inchworm:
1. Stand upright, then reach your hands down to the floor with your knees slightly bent.
2. Walk your hands forward into a plank, with your body in a straight line from shoulders to heels.
3. Pause for a moment, then walk your feet in small steps toward your hands.
4. Stand up fully and start the next rep.
Note: Brace your abs before you start walking your hands out, so your hips don't sag on the way to the plank.
exercises.squat-thrust:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, drop into a squat and place both hands on the floor.
2. Jump or step your feet back into a plank, with your body in a straight line.
3. Jump or step your feet back to your hands.
4. Stand up fully without a jump at the end, and start the next rep.
Note: If you have neighbors below or sensitive knees, step your feet instead of jumping; it's the same exercise without the noise and the impact.
exercises.frog-jump:
1. Stand with feet slightly wider than shoulder-width and toes turned slightly out.
2. Drop into a deep squat with a straight back and your hands between your feet.
3. Jump forward and up, and land back in a deep squat on both feet.
4. Keep going continuously forward over the distance you've cleared.
Note: If you can't reach a deep squat without rounding your back, go down only to the depth where your back stays straight, and shorten the jump.
exercises.jump-squat-180:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and drop into a half-squat.
2. Jump up powerfully, and in the air turn your body a half turn.
3. Land on both feet facing the opposite direction, and immediately drop into a half-squat to absorb.
4. Jump again and turn back to the original direction, alternating.
Note: The turn starts from your hips and shoulders together; don't turn only your upper body, and make sure the floor isn't slippery before you start.
exercises.marching-in-place:
1. Stand upright with feet hip-width apart and arms at your sides.
2. Lift one knee slightly off the floor and lower it, then switch to the other knee, like marching in place.
3. Move your arms gently in time with your legs, without jumping.
4. Keep a comfortable pace that lets you talk while moving.
Note: This is the quietest and gentlest entry version of the heart-rate movements; good for an initial warm-up or for sensitive knees.
exercises.stationary-bike:
1. Get on the bike and adjust the seat height so your knee stays slightly bent at the bottom of the pedal stroke.
2. Hold the handlebars and pedal at a steady, comfortable pace.
3. Keep your back upright and your breathing regular for the whole set time.
Note: Adjust the resistance so you can hold the pace for the entire item, without stopping.
exercises.treadmill-run:
1. Step onto the treadmill and start at a slow speed until you're steady.
2. Gradually increase to a walking or running speed according to your ability.
3. Keep your eyes forward and your torso upright, without hanging onto the handrails.
Careful: Slow down gradually at the end and don't step off the treadmill while it's still moving.
exercises.elliptical-trainer:
1. Step onto the machine, place your feet on the pedals, and grip the moving handles.
2. Push and move your legs in a smooth circular motion, with your arms moving in opposite coordination.
3. Keep a steady pace and an upright back for the whole set time.
Note: The movement is smooth with no impact; if you feel a thud with every step, slow down.
exercises.stair-climber-machine:
1. Step onto the machine and hold the side handles for balance only, without leaning on them.
2. Step at a steady pace as if climbing stairs, one step after another.
3. Keep your torso upright and eyes forward, without bending your back forward.
Note: Don't hang on the handles; your body weight should stay on your legs for the workout to be effective.
exercises.leg-press:
1. Sit with your back and hips against the backrest and your feet shoulder-width apart on the platform.
2. Release the safety lock and lower the platform slowly until your knees are bent to about 90 degrees.
3. Push through your heels until your legs are almost straight.
Note: Do not lock your knees or lift your hips off the seat as you lower the platform.
exercises.hack-squat:
1. Position your shoulders under the pads, your back against the backrest and your feet shoulder-width apart on the platform.
2. Release the handles and lower with control until your thighs are parallel to the platform.
3. Push through your heels to rise without locking your knees.
Note: Keep your back against the backrest throughout; do not let your pelvis roll away.
exercises.smith-squat:
1. Position the machine bar across your shoulders behind your head, with your feet a small step ahead of the bar.
2. Rotate the bar to unlock it and lower with control until your thighs are parallel to the floor.
3. Push through your heels to stand.
Note: The bar follows a fixed track. If your foot position feels unnatural, move your feet slightly forward.
exercises.leg-extension:
1. Sit with your back against the backrest and your ankles behind the lower pad.
2. Straighten your knees and lift the pad until your legs are almost straight.
3. Pause briefly, then lower slowly.
Note: Control the lowering; do not let the weights drop between repetitions.
exercises.hip-adduction:
1. Sit with your legs apart and the pads against the inside of your knees.
2. Bring your legs together with control.
3. Open slowly to a comfortable stretch, rather than your maximum range.
Note: Choose a comfortable opening range; avoid overstretching at the start of the set.
exercises.seated-leg-curl:
1. Sit with your legs straight over the lower pad and the upper pad secured against your thighs.
2. Bend your knees and pull the lower pad down and back as far as comfortable.
3. Return slowly until your legs are almost straight.
Note: Keep your hips against the seat. Reduce the weight if your pelvis lifts.
exercises.back-extension:
1. Position the support pads below your hips with your ankles secured behind you.
2. Cross your arms over your chest and lower your torso with control.
3. Raise your torso until it forms a straight line with your legs, without going beyond it.
Note: Stop at a straight line; excessive arching increases stress on the lower back.
exercises.pec-deck-fly:
1. Sit with your back against the backrest and your forearms or hands on the pads at chest height.
2. Bring your arms together in an arc until they meet in front of your chest.
3. Open slowly to a comfortable chest stretch.
Note: Use a comfortable range; do not let the weight pull your shoulders forcefully backward.
exercises.machine-shoulder-press:
1. Sit with the handles at shoulder height and your back against the backrest.
2. Press the handles upward until your arms are almost straight.
3. Lower slowly to ear height.
Note: Keep your lower back against the backrest; do not arch it to press more weight.
exercises.machine-row:
1. Sit with your chest against the front pad and hold the handles in both hands.
2. Pull the handles toward your body while bringing your shoulder blades together.
3. Return slowly until your arms are extended.
Note: Keep your chest against the pad. Reduce the weight if you need to lean backward to pull.
exercises.reverse-pec-deck:
1. Sit facing the pec-deck backrest with the handles in front of you at shoulder height.
2. Open your arms backward in a wide arc until they align with your shoulders.
3. Return slowly without releasing the tension.
Note: Move through your shoulders and shoulder blades; keep your elbows almost straight throughout.
exercises.hip-abduction:
1. Sit with your legs together and the pads against the outside of your knees.
2. Open your legs outward with control as far as comfortable.
3. Close slowly without swinging.
Note: Sit upright and hold the handles; do not lean backward to assist the movement.
exercises.machine-crunch:
1. Sit in the machine and hold the handles or place your chest against the pad, depending on the machine.
2. Curl your torso forward and downward using your abdomen, bringing your ribs toward your pelvis.
3. Return slowly to an upright seated position.
Note: Move through your abdomen; do not pull with your arms or bend only your neck.
exercises.calf-raise:
1. Stand in the machine with your shoulders under the pads and the balls of your feet on the step, with your heels unsupported.
2. Raise your heels as far as comfortable and pause briefly at the top.
3. Lower slowly below step height for a full stretch.
Note: Use your full comfortable range, upward and downward, without bouncing.
exercises.fedb-90-90-hamstring:
1. Lie on your back, with one leg extended straight out.
2. With the other leg, bend the hip and knee to 90 degrees. You may brace your leg with your hands if necessary. This will be your starting position.
3. Extend your leg straight into the air, pausing briefly at the top. Return the leg to the starting position.
4. Repeat for the repetitions shown in the workout, and then switch to the other leg.
5. Use the repetitions, hold time and load shown in this workout. Keep the movement controlled and within a comfortable range, using the apparatus and supports required above. Stop if pain occurs or technique deteriorates.
exercises.fedb-ab-roller:
1. Hold the Ab Roller with both hands and kneel on the floor.
2. Now place the ab roller on the floor in front of you so that you are on all your hands and knees (as in a kneeling push up position). This will be your starting position.
3. Slowly roll the ab roller straight forward, stretching your body into a straight position. Tip: Go down as far as you can without touching the floor with your body. Breathe in during this portion of the movement.
4. After a pause at the stretched position, start pulling yourself back to the starting position as you breathe out. Tip: Go slowly and keep your abs tight at all times.
5. Use the repetitions, hold time and load shown in this workout. Keep the movement controlled and within a comfortable range, using the apparatus and supports required above. Stop if pain occurs or technique deteriorates.
exercises.fedb-adductor:
1. Lie face down with one leg on a foam roll.
2. Rotate the leg so that the foam roll contacts against your inner thigh. Shift as much weight onto the foam roll as can be tolerated.
3. While trying to relax the muscles if the inner thigh, roll over the foam between your hip and knee, holding points of tension for 10-30 seconds. Repeat with the other leg.
4. Use the repetitions, hold time and load shown in this workout. Keep the movement controlled and within a comfortable range, using the apparatus and supports required above. Stop if pain occurs or technique deteriorates.
exercises.fedb-adductor-groin:
1. Lie on your back with your feet raised towards the ceiling.
2. Have your partner hold your feet or ankles. Abduct your legs as far as you can. This will be your starting position.
3. Attempt to squeeze your legs together for 10 or more seconds, while your partner prevents you from doing so.
4. Now, relax the muscles in your legs as your partner pushes your feet apart, stretching as far as is comfortable for you. Be sure to let your partner know when the stretch is adequate to prevent overstretching or injury.
5. Use the repetitions, hold time and load shown in this workout. Keep the movement controlled and within a comfortable range, using the apparatus and supports required above. Stop if pain occurs or technique deteriorates.
exercises.fedb-advanced-kettlebell-windmill:
1. Clean and press a kettlebell overhead with one arm.
2. Keeping the kettlebell locked out at all times, push your butt out in the direction of the locked out kettlebell. Keep the non-working arm behind your back and turn your feet out at a forty-five degree angle from the arm with the kettlebell.
3. Lower yourself as far as possible.
4. Pause for a second and reverse the motion back to the starting position.
5. Use the repetitions, hold time and load shown in this workout. Keep the movement controlled and within a comfortable range, using the apparatus and supports required above. Stop if pain occurs or technique deteriorates.
exercises.fedb-all-fours-quad-stretch:
1. Start off on your hands and knees, then lift your leg off the floor and hold the foot with your hand.
2. Use your hand to hold the foot or ankle, keeping the knee fully flexed, stretching the quadriceps and hip flexors.
3. Focus on extending your hips, thrusting them towards the floor. Hold for the hold time shown in the workout and then switch sides.
4. Use the repetitions, hold time and load shown in this workout. Keep the movement controlled and within a comfortable range, using the apparatus and supports required above. Stop if pain occurs or technique deteriorates.
exercises.fedb-alternate-hammer-curl:
1. Stand up with your torso upright and a dumbbell in each hand being held at arms length. The elbows should be close to the torso.
2. The palms of the hands should be facing your torso. This will be your starting position.
3. While holding the upper arm stationary, curl the right weight forward while contracting the biceps as you breathe out. Continue the movement until your biceps is fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level. Hold the contracted position for a second as you squeeze the biceps. Tip: Only the forearms should move.
4. Slowly begin to bring the dumbbells back to starting position as your breathe in.
5. Repeat the movement with the left hand. This equals one repetition.
6. Continue alternating in this manner for the recommended amount of repetitions.
7. Use the repetitions, hold time and load shown in this workout. Keep the movement controlled and within a comfortable range, using the apparatus and supports required above. Stop if pain occurs or technique deteriorates.
exercises.fedb-alternate-incline-dumbbell-curl:
1. Sit down on an incline bench with a dumbbell in each hand being held at arms length. Tip: Keep the elbows close to the torso.This will be your starting position.
2. While holding the upper arm stationary, curl the right weight forward while contracting the biceps as you breathe out. As you do so, rotate the hand so that the palm is facing up. Continue the movement until your biceps is fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level. Hold the contracted position for a second as you squeeze the biceps. Tip: Only the forearms should move.
3. Slowly begin to bring the dumbbell back to starting position as your breathe in.
4. Repeat the movement with the left hand. This equals one repetition.
5. Continue alternating in this manner for the recommended amount of repetitions.
6. Use the repetitions, hold time and load shown in this workout. Keep the movement controlled and within a comfortable range, using the apparatus and supports required above. Stop if pain occurs or technique deteriorates.
exercises.fedb-alternating-cable-shoulder-press:
1. Move the cables to the bottom of the tower and select an appropriate weight.
2. Grasp the cables and hold them at shoulder height, palms facing forward. This will be your starting position.
3. Keeping your head and chest up, extend through the elbow to press one side directly over head.
4. After pausing at the top, return to the starting position and repeat on the opposite side.
5. Use the repetitions, hold time and load shown in this workout. Keep the movement controlled and within a comfortable range, using the apparatus and supports required above. Stop if pain occurs or technique deteriorates.
exercises.fedb-alternating-deltoid-raise:
1. In a standing position, hold a pair of dumbbells at your side.
2. Keeping your elbows slightly bent, raise the weights directly in front of you to shoulder height, avoiding any swinging or cheating.
3. Return the weights to your side.
4. On the next repetition, raise the weights laterally, raising them out to your side to about shoulder height.
5. Return the weights to the starting position and continue alternating to the front and side.
6. Use the repetitions, hold time and load shown in this workout. Keep the movement controlled and within a comfortable range, using the apparatus and supports required above. Stop if pain occurs or technique deteriorates.
exercises.fedb-alternating-floor-press:
1. Lie on the floor with two kettlebells next to your shoulders.
2. Position one in place on your chest and then the other, gripping the kettlebells on the handle with the palms facing forward.
3. Extend both arms, so that the kettlebells are being held above your chest. Lower one kettlebell, bringing it to your chest and turn the wrist in the direction of the locked out kettlebell.
4. Raise the kettlebell and repeat on the opposite side.
5. Use the repetitions, hold time and load shown in this workout. Keep the movement controlled and within a comfortable range, using the apparatus and supports required above. Stop if pain occurs or technique deteriorates.
exercises.fedb-alternating-hang-clean:
1. Place two kettlebells between your feet. To get in the starting position, push your butt back and look straight ahead.
2. Clean one kettlebell to your shoulder and hold on to the other kettlebell in a hanging position. Clean the kettlebell to your shoulder by extending through the legs and hips as you pull the kettlebell towards your shoulders. Rotate your wrist as you do so.
3. Lower the cleaned kettlebell to a hanging position and clean the alternate kettlebell. Repeat.
4. Use the repetitions, hold time and load shown in this workout. Keep the movement controlled and within a comfortable range, using the apparatus and supports required above. Stop if pain occurs or technique deteriorates.
exercises.fedb-alternating-kettlebell-press:
1. Clean two kettlebells to your shoulders. Clean the kettlebells to your shoulders by extending through the legs and hips as you pull the kettlebells towards your shoulders. Rotate your wrists as you do so.
2. Press one directly overhead by extending through the elbow, turning it so the palm faces forward while holding the other kettlebell stationary .
3. Lower the pressed kettlebell to the starting position and immediately press with your other arm.
4. Use the repetitions, hold time and load shown in this workout. Keep the movement controlled and within a comfortable range, using the apparatus and supports required above. Stop if pain occurs or technique deteriorates.
exercises.fedb-alternating-kettlebell-row:
1. Place two kettlebells in front of your feet. Bend your knees slightly and push your butt out as much as possible. As you bend over to get into the starting position grab both kettlebells by the handles.
2. Pull one kettlebell off of the floor while holding on to the other kettlebell. Retract the shoulder blade of the working side, as you flex the elbow, drawing the kettlebell towards your stomach or rib cage.
3. Lower the kettlebell in the working arm and repeat with your other arm.
4. Use the repetitions, hold time and load shown in this workout. Keep the movement controlled and within a comfortable range, using the apparatus and supports required above. Stop if pain occurs or technique deteriorates.
exercises.fedb-ankle-circles:
1. Use a sturdy object like a squat rack to hold yourself.
2. Lift the right leg in the air (just around 2 inches from the floor) and perform a circular motion with the big toe. Pretend that you are drawing a big circle with it. Tip: One circle equals 1 repetition. Breathe normally as you perform the movement.
3. When you are done with the right foot, then repeat with the left leg.
4. Use the repetitions, hold time and load shown in this workout. Keep the movement controlled and within a comfortable range, using the apparatus and supports required above. Stop if pain occurs or technique deteriorates.
exercises.fedb-ankle-on-the-knee:
1. From a lying position, bend your knees and keep your feet on the floor.
2. Place your ankle of one foot on your opposite knee.
3. Grasp the thigh or knee of the bottom leg and pull both of your legs into the chest. Relax your neck and shoulders. Hold for the hold time shown in the workout and then switch sides.
4. Use the repetitions, hold time and load shown in this workout. Keep the movement controlled and within a comfortable range, using the apparatus and supports required above. Stop if pain occurs or technique deteriorates.
exercises.fedb-anterior-tibialis-smr:
1. Begin seated on the ground with your legs bent and your feet on the floor.
2. Using a Muscle Roller or a rolling pin, apply pressure to the muscles on the outside of your shins. Work from just below the knee to above the ankle, pausing at points of tension for 10-30 seconds. Repeat on the other leg.
3. Use the repetitions, hold time and load shown in this workout. Keep the movement controlled and within a comfortable range, using the apparatus and supports required above. Stop if pain occurs or technique deteriorates.
exercises.fedb-anti-gravity-press:
1. Place a bar on the ground behind the head of an incline bench.
2. Lay on the bench face down. With a pronated grip, pick the barbell up from the floor. Flex the elbows, performing a reverse curl to bring the bar near your chest. This will be your starting position.
3. To begin, press the barbell out in front of your head by extending your elbows. Keep your arms parallel to the ground throughout the movement.
4. Return to the starting position and repeat to complete the set.
5. Use the repetitions, hold time and load shown in this workout. Keep the movement controlled and within a comfortable range, using the apparatus and supports required above. Stop if pain occurs or technique deteriorates.
exercises.fedb-arm-circles:
1. Stand up and extend your arms straight out by the sides. The arms should be parallel to the floor and perpendicular (90-degree angle) to your torso. This will be your starting position.
2. Slowly start to make circles of about 1 foot in diameter with each outstretched arm. Breathe normally as you perform the movement.
3. Continue the circular motion of the outstretched arms for about ten seconds. Then reverse the movement, going the opposite direction.
4. Use the repetitions, hold time and load shown in this workout. Keep the movement controlled and within a comfortable range, using the apparatus and supports required above. Stop if pain occurs or technique deteriorates.
exercises.fedb-arnold-dumbbell-press:
1. Sit on an exercise bench with back support and hold two dumbbells in front of you at about upper chest level with your palms facing your body and your elbows bent. Tip: Your arms should be next to your torso. The starting position should look like the contracted portion of a dumbbell curl.
2. Now to perform the movement, raise the dumbbells as you rotate the palms of your hands until they are facing forward.
3. Continue lifting the dumbbells until your arms are extended above you in straight arm position. Breathe out as you perform this portion of the movement.
4. After a second pause at the top, begin to lower the dumbbells to the original position by rotating the palms of your hands towards you. Tip: The left arm will be rotated in a counter clockwise manner while the right one will be rotated clockwise. Breathe in as you perform this portion of the movement.
5. Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
6. Use the repetitions, hold time and load shown in this workout. Keep the movement controlled and within a comfortable range, using the apparatus and supports required above. Stop if pain occurs or technique deteriorates.
exercises.fedb-around-the-worlds:
1. Lay down on a flat bench holding a dumbbell in each hand with the palms of the hands facing towards the ceiling. Tip: Your arms should be parallel to the floor and next to your thighs. To avoid injury, make sure that you keep your elbows slightly bent. This will be your starting position.
2. Now move the dumbbells by creating a semi-circle as you displace them from the initial position to over the head. All of the movement should happen with the arms parallel to the floor at all times. Breathe in as you perform this portion of the movement.
3. Reverse the movement to return the weight to the starting position as you exhale.
4. Use the repetitions, hold time and load shown in this workout. Keep the movement controlled and within a comfortable range, using the apparatus and supports required above. Stop if pain occurs or technique deteriorates.
exercises.fedb-atlas-stone-trainer:
1. This trainer is effective for developing Atlas Stone strength for those who don't have access to stones, and are typically made from bar ends or heavy pipe.
2. Begin by loading the desired weight onto the bar. Straddle the weight, wrapping your arms around the implement, bending at the hips.
3. Begin by pulling the weight up past the knees, extending through the hips. As the weight clears the knees, it can be lapped by resting it on your thighs and sitting back, hugging it tightly to your chest.
4. Finish the movement by extending through your hips and knees to raise the weight as high as possible. The weight can be returned to the lap or to the ground for successive repetitions.
5. Use the repetitions, hold time and load shown in this workout. Keep the movement controlled and within a comfortable range, using the apparatus and supports required above. Stop if pain occurs or technique deteriorates.
exercises.fedb-atlas-stones:
1. Begin with the atlas stone between your feet. Bend at the hips to wrap your arms vertically around the Atlas Stone, attempting to get your fingers underneath the stone. Many stones will have a small flat portion on the bottom, which will make the stone easier to hold.
2. Pulling the stone into your torso, drive through the back half of your feet to pull the stone from the ground.
3. As the stone passes the knees, lap it by sitting backward, pulling the stone on top of your thighs.
4. Sit low, getting the stone high onto your chest as you change your grip to reach over the stone. Stand, driving through with your hips. Close distance to the loading platform, and lean back, extending the hips to get the stone as high as possible.
5. Use the repetitions, hold time and load shown in this workout. Keep the movement controlled and within a comfortable range, using the apparatus and supports required above. Stop if pain occurs or technique deteriorates.
exercises.fedb-axle-deadlift:
1. Approach the bar so that it is centered over your feet. You feet should be about hip width apart. Bend at the hip to grip the bar at shoulder width, allowing your shoulder blades to protract. Typically, you would use an over/under grip.
2. With your feet and your grip set, take a big breath and then lower your hips and flex the knees until your shins contact the bar. Look forward with your head, keep your chest up and your back arched, and begin driving through the heels to move the weight upward.
3. After the bar passes the knees, aggressively pull the bar back, pulling your shoulder blades together as you drive your hips forward into the bar.
4. Lower the bar by bending at the hips and guiding it to the floor.
5. Use the repetitions, hold time and load shown in this workout. Keep the movement controlled and within a comfortable range, using the apparatus and supports required above. Stop if pain occurs or technique deteriorates.
exercises.fedb-backward-drag:
1. Load a sled with the desired weight, attaching a rope or straps to the sled that you can hold onto.
2. Begin the exercise by moving backwards for a given distance. Leaning back, extend through the legs for short steps to move as quickly as possible.
3. Use the repetitions, hold time and load shown in this workout. Keep the movement controlled and within a comfortable range, using the apparatus and supports required above. Stop if pain occurs or technique deteriorates.
exercises.fedb-backward-medicine-ball-throw:
1. This exercise is best done with a partner. If you lack a partner, the ball can be thrown and retrieved or thrown against a wall.
2. Begin standing a few meters in front of your partner, both facing the same direction. Begin holding the ball between your legs.
3. Squat down and then forcefully reverse direction, coming to full extension and you toss the ball over your head to your partner.
4. Your partner can then roll the ball back to you. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
5. Use the repetitions, hold time and load shown in this workout. Keep the movement controlled and within a comfortable range, using the apparatus and supports required above. Stop if pain occurs or technique deteriorates.
exercises.fedb-balance-board:
1. Place a balance board in front of you.
2. Stand up on it and try to balance yourself.
3. Hold the balance for as long as desired.
4. Use the repetitions, hold time and load shown in this workout. Keep the movement controlled and within a comfortable range, using the apparatus and supports required above. Stop if pain occurs or technique deteriorates.
exercises.fedb-ball-leg-curl:
1. Begin on the floor laying on your back with your feet on top of the ball.
2. Position the ball so that when your legs are extended your ankles are on top of the ball. This will be your starting position.
3. Raise your hips off of the ground, keeping your weight on the shoulder blades and your feet.
4. Flex the knees, pulling the ball as close to you as you can, contracting the hamstrings.
5. After a brief pause, return to the starting position.
6. Use the repetitions, hold time and load shown in this workout. Keep the movement controlled and within a comfortable range, using the apparatus and supports required above. Stop if pain occurs or technique deteriorates.
exercises.fedb-barbell-ab-rollout-on-knees:
1. Hold an Olympic barbell loaded with 5-10lbs on each side and kneel on the floor.
2. Now place the barbell on the floor in front of you so that you are on all your hands and knees (as in a kneeling push up position). This will be your starting position.
3. Slowly roll the barbell straight forward, stretching your body into a straight position. Tip: Go down as far as you can without touching the floor with your body. Breathe in during this portion of the movement.
4. After a second pause at the stretched position, start pulling yourself back to the starting position as you breathe out. Tip: Go slowly and keep your abs tight at all times.
5. Use the repetitions, hold time and load shown in this workout. Keep the movement controlled and within a comfortable range, using the apparatus and supports required above. Stop if pain occurs or technique deteriorates.
exercises.fedb-barbell-curl:
1. Stand up with your torso upright while holding a barbell at a shoulder-width grip. The palm of your hands should be facing forward and the elbows should be close to the torso. This will be your starting position.
2. While holding the upper arms stationary, curl the weights forward while contracting the biceps as you breathe out. Tip: Only the forearms should move.
3. Continue the movement until your biceps are fully contracted and the bar is at shoulder level. Hold the contracted position for a second and squeeze the biceps hard.
4. Slowly begin to bring the bar back to starting position as your breathe in.
5. Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
6. Use the repetitions, hold time and load shown in this workout. Keep the movement controlled and within a comfortable range, using the apparatus and supports required above. Stop if pain occurs or technique deteriorates.
exercises.fedb-barbell-curls-lying-against-an-incl:
1. Lie against an incline bench, with your arms holding a barbell and hanging down in a horizontal line. This will be your starting position.
2. While keeping the upper arms stationary, curl the weight up as high as you can while squeezing the biceps. Breathe out as you perform this portion of the movement. Tip: Only the forearms should move. Do not swing the arms.
3. After a second contraction, slowly go back to the starting position as you inhale. Tip: Make sure that you go all of the way down.
4. Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
5. Use the repetitions, hold time and load shown in this workout. Keep the movement controlled and within a comfortable range, using the apparatus and supports required above. Stop if pain occurs or technique deteriorates.
exercises.fedb-barbell-full-squat:
1. This exercise is best performed inside a squat rack for safety purposes. To begin, first set the bar on a rack just above shoulder level. Once the correct height is chosen and the bar is loaded, step under the bar and place the back of your shoulders (slightly below the neck) across it.
2. Hold on to the bar using both arms at each side and lift it off the rack by first pushing with your legs and at the same time straightening your torso.
3. Step away from the rack and position your legs using a shoulder-width medium stance with the toes slightly pointed out. Keep your head up at all times and maintain a straight back. This will be your starting position.
4. Begin to slowly lower the bar by bending the knees and sitting back with your hips as you maintain a straight posture with the head up. Continue down until your hamstrings are on your calves. Inhale as you perform this portion of the movement.
5. Begin to raise the bar as you exhale by pushing the floor with the heel or middle of your foot as you straighten the legs and extend the hips to go back to the starting position.
6. Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
7. Use the repetitions, hold time and load shown in this workout. Keep the movement controlled and within a comfortable range, using the apparatus and supports required above. Stop if pain occurs or technique deteriorates.
exercises.fedb-barbell-guillotine-bench-press:
1. Using a medium width grip (a grip that creates a 90-degree angle in the middle of the movement between the forearms and the upper arms), lift the bar from the rack and hold it straight over your neck with your arms locked. This will be your starting position.
2. As you breathe in, bring the bar down slowly until it is about 1 inch from your neck.
3. After a second pause, bring the bar back to the starting position as you breathe out and push the bar using your chest muscles. Lock your arms and squeeze your chest in the contracted position, hold for a second and then start coming down slowly again. It should take at least twice as long to go down than to come up.
4. Repeat the movement for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
5. When you are done, place the bar back in the rack.
6. Use the repetitions, hold time and load shown in this workout. Keep the movement controlled and within a comfortable range, using the apparatus and supports required above. Stop if pain occurs or technique deteriorates.
exercises.fedb-barbell-hack-squat:
1. Stand up straight while holding a barbell behind you at arms length and your feet at shoulder width. Tip: A shoulder width grip is best with the palms of your hands facing back. You can use wrist wraps for this exercise for a better grip. This will be your starting position.
2. While keeping your head and eyes up and back straight, squat until your upper thighs are parallel to the floor. Breathe in as you slowly go down.
3. Pressing mainly with the heel of the foot and squeezing the thighs, go back up as you breathe out.
4. Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
5. Use the repetitions, hold time and load shown in this workout. Keep the movement controlled and within a comfortable range, using the apparatus and supports required above. Stop if pain occurs or technique deteriorates.
exercises.fedb-barbell-incline-shoulder-raise:
1. Lie back on an Incline Bench. Using a medium width grip (a grip that is slightly wider than shoulder width), lift the bar from the rack and hold it straight over you with your arms straight. This will be your starting position.
2. While keeping the arms straight, lift the bar by protracting your shoulder blades, raising the shoulders from the bench as you breathe out.
3. Bring back the bar to the starting position as you breathe in.
4. Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
5. Use the repetitions, hold time and load shown in this workout. Keep the movement controlled and within a comfortable range, using the apparatus and supports required above. Stop if pain occurs or technique deteriorates.
exercises.fedb-barbell-lunge:
1. This exercise is best performed inside a squat rack for safety purposes. To begin, first set the bar on a rack just below shoulder level. Once the correct height is chosen and the bar is loaded, step under the bar and place the back of your shoulders (slightly below the neck) across it.
2. Hold on to the bar using both arms at each side and lift it off the rack by first pushing with your legs and at the same time straightening your torso.
3. Step away from the rack and step forward with your right leg and squat down through your hips, while keeping the torso upright and maintaining balance. Inhale as you go down. Note: Do not allow your knee to go forward beyond your toes as you come down, as this will put undue stress on the knee joint. li>
4. Using mainly the heel of your foot, push up and go back to the starting position as you exhale.
5. Repeat the movement for the recommended amount of repetitions and then perform with the left leg.
6. Use the repetitions, hold time and load shown in this workout. Keep the movement controlled and within a comfortable range, using the apparatus and supports required above. Stop if pain occurs or technique deteriorates.
exercises.fedb-barbell-rear-delt-row:
1. Stand up straight while holding a barbell using a wide (higher than shoulder width) and overhand (palms facing your body) grip.
2. Bend knees slightly and bend over as you keep the natural arch of your back. Let the arms hang in front of you as they hold the bar. Once your torso is parallel to the floor, flare the elbows out and away from your body. Tip: Your torso and your arms should resemble the letter "T". Now you are ready to begin the exercise.
3. While keeping the upper arms perpendicular to the torso, pull the barbell up towards your upper chest as you squeeze the rear delts and you breathe out. Tip: When performed correctly, this exercise should resemble a bench press in reverse. Also, refrain from using your biceps to do the work. Focus on targeting the rear delts; the arms should only act as hooks.
4. Slowly go back to the initial position as you breathe in.
5. Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
6. Use the repetitions, hold time and load shown in this workout. Keep the movement controlled and within a comfortable range, using the apparatus and supports required above. Stop if pain occurs or technique deteriorates.
exercises.fedb-barbell-rollout-from-bench:
1. Place a loaded barbell on the ground, near the end of a bench. Kneel with both legs on the bench, and take a medium to narrow grip on the barbell. This will be your starting position.
2. To begin, extend through the hips to slowly roll the bar forward. As you roll out, flex the shoulder to roll the bar above your head. Ensure that your arms remain extended throughout the movement.
3. When the bar has been moved as far forward as possible, return to the starting position.
4. Use the repetitions, hold time and load shown in this workout. Keep the movement controlled and within a comfortable range, using the apparatus and supports required above. Stop if pain occurs or technique deteriorates.
exercises.fedb-barbell-seated-calf-raise:
1. Place a block about 12 inches in front of a flat bench.
2. Sit on the bench and place the ball of your feet on the block.
3. Have someone place a barbell over your upper thighs about 3 inches above your knees and hold it there. This will be your starting position.
4. Raise up on your toes as high as possible as you squeeze the calves and as you breathe out.
5. After a second contraction, slowly go back to the starting position. Tip: To get maximum benefit stretch your calves as far as you can.
6. Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
7. Use the repetitions, hold time and load shown in this workout. Keep the movement controlled and within a comfortable range, using the apparatus and supports required above. Stop if pain occurs or technique deteriorates.
exercises.fedb-barbell-shrug-behind-the-back:
1. Stand up straight with your feet at shoulder width as you hold a barbell with both hands behind your back using a pronated grip (palms facing back). Tip: Your hands should be a little wider than shoulder width apart. You can use wrist wraps for this exercise for better grip. This will be your starting position.
2. Raise your shoulders up as far as you can go as you breathe out and hold the contraction for a second. Tip: Refrain from trying to lift the barbell by using your biceps. The arms should remain stretched out at all times.
3. Slowly return to the starting position as you breathe in.
4. Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
5. Use the repetitions, hold time and load shown in this workout. Keep the movement controlled and within a comfortable range, using the apparatus and supports required above. Stop if pain occurs or technique deteriorates.
exercises.fedb-barbell-side-bend:
1. Stand up straight while holding a barbell placed on the back of your shoulders (slightly below the neck). Your feet should be shoulder width apart. This will be your starting position.
2. While keeping your back straight and your head up, bend only at the waist to the right as far as possible. Breathe in as you bend to the side. Then hold for a second and come back up to the starting position as you exhale. Tip: Keep the rest of the body stationary.
3. Now repeat the movement but bending to the left instead. Hold for a second and come back to the starting position.
4. Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
5. Use the repetitions, hold time and load shown in this workout. Keep the movement controlled and within a comfortable range, using the apparatus and supports required above. Stop if pain occurs or technique deteriorates.
exercises.fedb-barbell-side-split-squat:
1. Stand up straight while holding a barbell placed on the back of your shoulders (slightly below the neck). Your feet should be placed wide apart with the foot of the lead leg angled out to the side. This will be your starting position.
2. Lower your body towards the side of your angled foot by bending the knee and hip of your lead leg and while keeping the opposite leg only slightly bent. Breathe in as you lower your body.
3. Return to the starting position by extending the hip and knee of the lead leg. Breathe out as you perform this movement.
4. After performing the recommended amount of reps, repeat the movement with the opposite leg.
5. Use the repetitions, hold time and load shown in this workout. Keep the movement controlled and within a comfortable range, using the apparatus and supports required above. Stop if pain occurs or technique deteriorates.
exercises.fedb-barbell-squat-to-a-bench:
1. This exercise is best performed inside a squat rack for safety purposes. To begin, first place a flat bench or a box behind you. The flat bench is used to teach you to set your hips back and to hit depth.
2. 
3. Then, set the bar on a rack that best matches your height. Once the correct height is chosen and the bar is loaded, step under the bar and place the back of your shoulders (slightly below the neck) across it.
4. Hold on to the bar using both arms at each side and lift it off the rack by first pushing with your legs and at the same time straightening your torso.
5. Step away from the rack and position your legs using a shoulder width medium stance with the toes slightly pointed out. Keep your head up at all times as looking down will get you off balance and also maintain a straight back. This will be your starting position. (Note: For the purposes of this discussion we will use the medium stance described above which targets overall development; however you can choose any of the three stances discussed in the foot stances section).
6. Begin to slowly lower the bar by bending the knees and sitting your hips back as you maintain a straight posture with the head up. Continue down until you slightly touch the bench behind you. Inhale as you perform this portion of the movement. Tip: If you performed the exercise correctly, the front of the knees should make an imaginary straight line with the toes that is perpendicular to the front. If your knees are past that imaginary line (if they are past your toes) then you are placing undue stress on the knee and the exercise has been performed incorrectly.
7. Begin to raise the bar as you exhale by pushing the floor with the heel of your foot as you straighten the legs and extend the hips to go back to the starting position.
8. Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
9. Use the repetitions, hold time and load shown in this workout. Keep the movement controlled and within a comfortable range, using the apparatus and supports required above. Stop if pain occurs or technique deteriorates.
exercises.fedb-barbell-step-ups:
1. Stand up straight while holding a barbell placed on the back of your shoulders (slightly below the neck) and stand upright behind an elevated platform (such as the one used for spotting behind a flat bench). This is your starting position.
